knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Valued Toland Conjugate Pair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal and Fenchel-conjugate DC minimization families for finite convex components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be finite convex functions. Define
\[
(P)\quad\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{g(x)-h(x)\},
\qquad
(D)\quad\inf_{y\in\operatorname{dom}h^*}\{h^*(y)-g^*(y)\}.
\]
Then their values agree in the extended-real sense:
\[
\inf(P)=\inf(D).
\]
If \(y\in\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\), their objective values agree at that pair:
\[
g(x)-h(x)=h^*(y)-g^*(y).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-valued DC minimization problem and its reversed-conjugate DC problem have the same extended optimal value; common subgradients match their objective values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_x(g-h)=\inf_{y\in\operatorname{dom}h^*}(h^*-g^*)\), with paired equality at common subgradients.

notation.meaning: primal and conjugate-dual DC problem families

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Valued Toland Conjugate Pair
DC Primal-Dual Problem Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Toland–Singer conjugate pairing for unconstrained DC programs, including constraints through indicator functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), the DC primal and conjugate dual families are
\[
(P)\quad \inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{g(x)-h(x)\},
\qquad
(D)\quad \inf_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{h^*(y)-g^*(y)\}.
\]
Whenever Toland–Singer duality applies, their optimal values coincide. Moreover, if \(y\in\partial g(x)\cap\partial h(x)\), Fenchel equalities give
\[
g(x)-h(x)=h^*(y)-g^*(y).
\]
A constrained problem on a closed convex set \(C\) is included by replacing \(g\) with \(g+\iota_C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DC minimization problem has a conjugate DC dual obtained by reversing the conjugates; common subgradients identify equal primal and dual objective values.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
The relevant primal and dual values are finite and the stated Toland–Singer qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf(g-h)=\inf(h^*-g^*)\), with equal paired objective values at common subgradients.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Loss of Nonclosed Quasiconvex Sublevels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of exact support recovery without lower semicontinuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) by \(f(x)=0\) for \(x>0\) and \(f(x)=1\) for \(x\le0\). Then \(f\) is quasiconvex but not lower-semicontinuous, and
\[
\{x:f(x)\le0\}=(0,\infty).
\]
The intersection of all closed halfspaces containing this sublevel set is \([0,\infty)\), so its support values recover the closure rather than the original sublevel set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without lower semicontinuity, support-halfspace reconstruction can close a nonclosed quasiconvex sublevel set and fail to recover the function exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Support-function reconstruction need not recover a nonclosed quasiconvex sublevel set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Level-Set Support Quasiconjugacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A specified support-function convention for representing lower-semicontinuous quasiconvex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and quasiconvex. For \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\), define
\[
Q_f(y,\alpha)=\sup\{\langle y,z\rangle:f(z)\le\alpha\},
\]
with \(\sup\varnothing=-\infty\). Then
\[
\{x:f(x)\le\alpha\}=\bigcap_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{x:\langle y,x\rangle\le Q_f(y,\alpha)\},
\]
and
\[
f(x)=\inf\{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}:\langle y,x\rangle\le Q_f(y,\alpha)\ \forall y\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated convention, a lower-semicontinuous quasiconvex function is recovered from the support functions of its closed convex sublevel sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every sublevel set, and hence \(f\), is recovered from \(Q_f\).

notation.meaning: support function of the alpha-sublevel set

knowledge_statements.title: Level-Set Support Quasiconjugacy
Quasiconjugate Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level-set support quasiconjugacy for proper lower-semicontinuous quasiconvex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and quasiconvex. Define its level-set quasiconjugate by
\[
Q_f(y,\alpha)=\sup\{\langle y,x\rangle:f(x)\le\alpha\}.
\]
Every nonempty sublevel set is recovered from these values as
\[
\{x:f(x)\le\alpha\}
=
\bigcap_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}
\{x:\langle y,x\rangle\le Q_f(y,\alpha)\}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
f(x)=\inf\{\alpha:\langle y,x\rangle\le Q_f(y,\alpha)\ \text{for every }y\in\mathbb{R}^n\},
\]
with the infimum interpreted in the extended-real sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-semicontinuous quasiconvex function is represented by the support functions of its convex sublevel sets, yielding a level-set form of quasiconjugate duality.
assumptions_latex: The represented sublevel set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sublevel sets, and hence \(f\), are recovered from \(Q_f\).

notation.meaning: support-function quasiconjugate of the alpha-sublevel set

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasi-Supgradient and Quasi-Supdifferential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A generalized supergradient notion defined through quasiconjugate equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{\pm\infty\}\), a vector \(p\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\) is a quasi-supgradient of \(f\) at \(x\) if
\[
p^Tx=1\quad\text{and}\quad f(x)f^{\natural}(p)\ge1.
\]
Because \(f(x)f^{\natural}(p)\le1\), this is equivalently
\[
p^Tx=1\quad\text{and}\quad f(x)f^{\natural}(p)=1.
\]
The quasi-supdifferential is
\[
\partial^{\natural}f(x)=\{p\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\mid p^Tx=1,\ f(x)f^{\natural}(p)=1\}.
\]
The function is quasi-supdifferentiable at \(x\) when \(\partial^{\natural}f(x)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative vector p is a quasi-supgradient at x when p transpose x equals one and the product of f(x) with the quasiconjugate at p equals one. The set of all such vectors is the quasi-supdifferential, and f is quasi-supdifferentiable at x when this set is nonempty.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasiconjugate of an extended-real-valued function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of the quasiconjugation operation used in the supplied DC-global-optimization duality framework.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), its quasiconjugate \(f^H:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is defined by \[f^H(y)=\begin{cases}-\inf\{f(x):\langle x,y\rangle\ge 1\},&y\neq0,\\-\sup\{f(x):x\in\mathbb R^n\},&y=0.\end{cases}\] When \(\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)=+\infty\), this can be written for every \(y\) as \[f^H(y)=-\inf\{f(x):\langle x,y\rangle\ge1\}.\]

At zero, it is minus the global supremum of f. If that supremum is positive infinity, the first formula also yields the zero value under extended-real conventions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Properties and Recovery Formula for the Quasiconjugate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural properties of quasiconjugation and recovery of a continuous increasing quasiconcave function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}_+^n\to\mathbb{R}_+\) be nonzero and let \(f^{\natural}\) be its quasiconjugate. Then \(f^{\natural}\) is quasiconcave, nonnegative, and increasing on \(\mathbb{R}_+^n\), and
\[
f^{\natural}(0)=\inf\{f^{\natural}(y)\mid y\in\mathbb{R}^n\}.
\]
If, in addition, \(f\) is quasiconcave, continuous, and increasing on \(\mathbb{R}_+^n\), then for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\),
\[
f(x)=\frac{1}{\sup\{f^{\natural}(p)\mid p^Tx\le1,\ p\ge0\}}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quasiconjugate is nonnegative, quasiconcave, and increasing, with its infimum attained at zero. If the original function is also continuous, quasiconcave, and increasing, it is recovered by applying the reciprocal-supremum construction to its quasiconjugate.
assumptions_latex: \text{For the recovery formula, }f\text{ is quasiconcave, continuous, and increasing on }\mathbb{R}_+^n.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is sup-coercive if, for every sequence \((x^k)\subset\mathbb R^n\), \[\|x^k\|\to+\infty\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f(x^k)\to\sup\{f(x):x\in\mathbb R^n\}.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quasiconvexity and regularity of the quasiconjugate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three properties of quasiconjugation, with the distinct hypotheses for sup-coercivity and each semicontinuity implication preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\), and let \(f^H\) be its quasiconjugate. Then: (i) \(f^H\) is quasiconvex and \(f^H(0)=\inf\{f^H(y):y\in\mathbb R^n\}\); (ii) if \(\lim_{x\to0}f(x)=f(0)=\inf\{f(x):x\in\mathbb R^n\}\), then \(f^H\) is sup-coercive; (iii) if \(f\) is upper semicontinuous, then \(f^H\) is lower semicontinuous, and if \(f\) is lower semicontinuous and sup-coercive, then \(f^H\) is upper semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every quasiconjugate is quasiconvex, and its value at zero equals its global infimum. If f converges at the origin to its globally minimal value there, its quasiconjugate is sup-coercive. Upper semicontinuity of f implies lower semicontinuity of the quasiconjugate; lower semicontinuity and sup-coercivity of f imply upper semicontinuity of the quasiconjugate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^H\text{ is quasiconvex},\quad f^H(0)=\inf_{y\in\mathbb R^n}f^H(y),\quad [\lim_{x\to0}f(x)=f(0)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\Rightarrow f^H\text{ is sup-coercive}],\quad [f\text{ usc}\Rightarrow f^H\text{ lsc}],\quad [f\text{ lsc and sup-coercive}\Rightarrow f^H\text{ usc}].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Common-Subgradient DC Dual Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal optimality certified by an attained conjugate-dual value and Fenchel equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be finite convex functions, and consider
\[
(P)=\inf_x\{g(x)-h(x)\},\qquad (D)=\inf_{y\in\operatorname{dom}h^*}\{h^*(y)-g^*(y)\}.
\]
If \(\bar y\) globally minimizes \((D)\) and
\[
\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x),
\]
then
\[
g(\bar x)-h(\bar x)=h^*(\bar y)-g^*(\bar y)=\inf(P),
\]
so \(\bar x\) is a global primal minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally optimal conjugate-dual point sharing both convex subgradients with a primal point certifies exact primal global optimality and zero conjugate gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}(g-h)\) and the displayed primal and dual values coincide.
knowledge_statements.title: Common-Subgradient DC Dual Certificate
DC Dual-Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global optimality certificate formed by a conjugate-dual minimizer and Fenchel equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the Toland pair \((P)\) and \((D)\) for proper lower-semicontinuous convex \(g,h\), under equality of their finite optimal values. A pair \((\bar x,\bar y)\) certifies global primal optimality if
\[
\bar y\in\partial g(\bar x)\cap\partial h(\bar x)
\quad\text{and}\quad
h^*(\bar y)-g^*(\bar y)
\le h^*(y)-g^*(y)
\quad\text{for every }y.
\]
The common-subgradient relations are directly checked by Fenchel equalities, and they imply
\[
g(\bar x)-h(\bar x)=h^*(\bar y)-g^*(\bar y)=\inf(P).
\]
Thus the dual optimum and zero conjugate gap certify the primal bound exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual global minimizer sharing both convex subgradients with a primal point certifies that point’s global DC optimality through zero conjugate gap.
assumptions_latex: Toland duality holds with a finite common optimal value.
\(g\) and \(h\) are proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}(g-h)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Product relaxation for bounded convex or concave factors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine max/min formulas for products whose factors have known nonnegative ranges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let p\ge0 and r\ge0. If u:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} and v:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R} are finite and convex, then on
\[
D=\{(x,y):p\le u(x)\le q,\ r\le v(y)\le s\}
\]
the function
\[
\max\{r u(x)+p v(y)-pr,\ s u(x)+q v(y)-qs\}
\]
is a convex minorant of u(x)v(y). If instead u and v are finite and concave, then on D the function
\[
\min\{s u(x)+p v(y)-ps,\ r u(x)+q v(y)-qr\}
\]
is a concave majorant of u(x)v(y).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative bounded factors, the maximum of two affine combinations gives a convex product underestimator when both factors are convex; dually, the minimum of two affine combinations gives a concave product overestimator when both are concave.
assumptions_latex: u\text{ and }v\text{ are finite on }\mathbb{R}^n\text{ and }\mathbb{R}^m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max\{ru+pv-pr,su+qv-qs\}\le uv\quad\text{in the convex case},\qquad uv\le\min\{su+pv-ps,ru+qv-qr\}\quad\text{in the concave case}.

For real numbers p<q and r<s, the conditions p\le u\le q and r\le v\le s are equivalent to

uv\le\min\{su+pv-ps,\;ru+qv-qr\}

uv\ge\max\{ru+pv-pr,\;su+qv-qs\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Product relaxation from separate factor bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses convex lower bounds and concave upper bounds for two nonnegative bounded factors on a convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m be convex, p\ge0, and r\ge0. Suppose \varphi,\psi are convex and \Phi,\Psi are concave, with
\[
p\le\varphi(x)\le u(x)\le\Phi(x)\le q,
\qquad
r\le\psi(y)\le v(y)\le\Psi(y)\le s
\]
for every (x,y)\in D. Then
\[
\max\{r\varphi(x)+p\psi(y)-pr,\ s\varphi(x)+q\psi(y)-qs\}
\]
is a convex minorant of u(x)v(y) on D, and
\[
\min\{s\Phi(x)+p\Psi(y)-ps,\ r\Phi(x)+q\Psi(y)-qr\}
\]
is a concave majorant of u(x)v(y) on D.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex lower relaxations and concave upper relaxations of two nonnegative factors can be combined through the bilinear rectangle formulas to produce convex and concave relaxations of their product.
assumptions_latex: p\le\varphi\le u\le\Phi\le q\text{ and }r\le\psi\le v\le\Psi\le s\text{ on }D
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max\{r\varphi+p\psi-pr,s\varphi+q\psi-qs\}\le uv\le\min\{s\Phi+p\Psi-ps,r\Phi+q\Psi-qr\}\quad\text{on }D.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Minorants of DC Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex lower bounds obtained from concave majorization of the subtracted component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f=g-h\) on a convex set \(C\), where \(g,h:C\to\mathbb{R}\) are convex. If \(U:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is concave and satisfies \(U(x)\ge h(x)\) for every \(x\in C\), then
\[
m_U(x)=g(x)-U(x)
\]
is convex on \(C\) and obeys
\[
m_U(x)\le f(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in C.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\inf_{x\in C}m_U(x)\le\inf_{x\in C}f(x),
\]
so minimizing \(m_U\) supplies a valid global lower bound for the DC problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting any concave upper estimator of the second convex component from the first component produces a convex minorant and a valid global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_U=g-U\) is convex, \(m_U\le g-h\), and \(\inf_Cm_U\le\inf_C(g-h)\).

notation.meaning: induced convex minorant of the DC objective

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=g-h\) and \(m_U=g-U\) on \(C\), where \(U\ge h\). Then \[f(x)-m_U(x)=U(x)-h(x)\ge0.\] Thus \(m_U(x)=f(x)\) exactly when \(U(x)=h(x)\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongest Fixed-Decomposition Majorant Minorant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise strongest member of the family induced by concave majorants of the subtracted component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(f=g-h\), where \(g,h\) are finite convex functions and \(h\) is continuous on \(C\). Define \[\operatorname{cav}_C h(x)=\sup\left\{\sum_{i=1}^r\lambda_i h(x_i):\lambda_i\ge0,\ \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\ \sum_i\lambda_i x_i=x,\ x_i\in C\right\}.\] This is the least concave majorant of \(h\) on \(C\). Hence \(m^*=g-\operatorname{cav}_C h\) is convex and, for every concave majorant \(U\ge h\), \[g-U\le m^*\le g-h\quad\text{on }C.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed DC decomposition on a compact convex set, subtracting the least concave majorant of the second component gives the pointwise strongest minorant obtainable by this construction.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
\(g\) and \(h\) are finite convex functions on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g-U\le g-\operatorname{cav}_C h\le g-h\quad\text{for every concave }U\ge h.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex relaxation and DC minorant on a polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines relaxation by a convex minorant and records the explicit minorant induced by a known DC decomposition on a polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be convex and let c be convex on D with c(x)\le f(x) for every x\in D. Then c(x)\le0 is a convex relaxation of f(x)\le0 on D. The tightest relaxation of this form uses c=\operatorname{conv}_D f, the largest convex minorant of f on D. If D=\operatorname{conv}(V) is a polytope and f=g-h with g and h convex, then
\[
g(x)+\operatorname{conv}_D(-h)(x)=g(x)-\sup\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{n+1}\lambda_i h(v^i):v^i\in V,\ \lambda_i\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^{n+1}\lambda_i=1,\ \sum_{i=1}^{n+1}\lambda_i v^i=x\right\}
\]
is a convex minorant of f on D.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex minorant yields a convex relaxation of a nonconvex inequality, with the convex envelope giving the tightest such relaxation. For a known DC decomposition on a polytope, a convex minorant is obtained from the convex envelope of the negative convex component.
assumptions_latex: c\text{ is convex on }D\text{ and }c(x)\le f(x)\text{ for all }x\in D
\text{For the explicit construction, }D=\operatorname{conv}(V)\text{ is a polytope and }f=g-h\text{ with }g,h\text{ convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x\in D:f(x)\le0\}\subseteq\{x\in D:c(x)\le0\},\qquad g+\operatorname{conv}_D(-h)\le f\text{ on }D.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral DC Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplexwise polyhedral underestimation using vertex interpolation of the subtracted convex component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\}\) be a simplex and write each \(x\in S\) uniquely as \(x=\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i(x)v_i\), where \(\lambda_i(x)\ge0\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i(x)=1\). For convex \(h\), define
\[
U_S(x)=\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i(x)h(v_i).
\]
Convexity gives \(h(x)\le U_S(x)\). Hence, for \(f=g-h\),
\[
m_S(x)=g(x)-U_S(x)\le f(x)\quad(x\in S).
\]
The function \(U_S\) is affine; if \(g\) is polyhedral convex, then \(m_S\) is a polyhedral convex underestimator on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vertex interpolation upper-bounds the subtracted convex component on a simplex, producing a valid underestimator that is polyhedral convex when the first component is polyhedral convex.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are convex and finite on \(S\).
\(g\) is polyhedral when polyhedrality of \(m_S\) is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_S=g-U_S\le g-h\) on \(S\), and \(m_S\) is polyhedral convex when \(g\) is polyhedral convex.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone Refinement and Uniform Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation properties of piecewise-affine vertex-interpolation DC underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a compact polytope, let \(h:P\to\mathbb R\) be continuous and convex, and let \(\mathcal T'\) be a conforming refinement of a finite triangulation \(\mathcal T\). If \(U_{\mathcal T}\) and \(U_{\mathcal T'}\) are the piecewise-affine vertex interpolants of \(h\), then \(h\le U_{\mathcal T'}\le U_{\mathcal T}\) on \(P\). Thus, for \(f=g-h\), \(g-U_{\mathcal T}\le g-U_{\mathcal T'}\le f\). For triangulations \(\mathcal T_k\) whose maximum simplex diameter tends to zero, \(\|U_{\mathcal T_k}-h\|_\infty\to0\), and hence \(\|f-(g-U_{\mathcal T_k})\|_\infty\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conforming refinement monotonically strengthens vertex-interpolation underestimators, and vanishing mesh makes them uniformly exact.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is finite, continuous, and convex on \(P\).
Monotonicity uses a conforming refinement; consistency uses maximum simplex diameter tending to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The refined underestimator dominates the coarse one, and vanishing mesh yields uniform convergence to \(f\).

notation.meaning: piecewise-affine vertex interpolant on triangulation \(\mathcal T\)

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition-Dependent Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity is decomposition invariant, but numerical strength depends on the chosen DC decomposition and majorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the same objective has two DC decompositions
\[
f=g-h=(g+\phi)-(h+\phi),
\]
where \(g,h,\phi\) are convex on \(C\). Let \(U\ge h\) and \(\widetilde U\ge h+\phi\) be concave majorants on \(C\). Their valid lower bounds are
\[
L=\inf_{x\in C}\{g(x)-U(x)\},
\qquad
\widetilde L=\inf_{x\in C}\{g(x)+\phi(x)-\widetilde U(x)\}.
\]
Both satisfy \(L,\widetilde L\le\inf_C f\), but neither ordering \(L\le\widetilde L\) nor \(\widetilde L\le L\) follows without an ordering between \(U\) and \(\widetilde U-\phi\). Thus bound strength is decomposition dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding the same convex function to both DC components preserves the objective but can strengthen or weaken lower bounds because the required majorant changes.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h,\phi\) are convex on a nonempty convex set \(C\).
\(U\) and \(\widetilde U\) are the stated concave majorants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both bounds are valid, while their relative strength requires comparing \(U\) with \(\widetilde U-\phi\).

notation.meaning: lower bounds from two DC decompositions
convex function added to both components

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reversal of Decomposition-Bound Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of any decomposition-independent ordering of valid DC lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(C=[0,1]\), let \(f\equiv0\). For \(f=0-0\), the concave majorant \(U\equiv1\) gives \(L=-1\). For the equivalent decomposition \(f=x^2-x^2\), the affine secant majorant \(\widetilde U(x)=x\) gives \(\widetilde L=\min_{[0,1]}(x^2-x)=-1/4>L\). Replacing \(U\) by the valid majorant \(U\equiv0\) gives \(L=0>\widetilde L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent DC decompositions can yield either ordering of their valid lower bounds, depending on the selected majorants.
assumptions_latex: Each selected majorant is concave and pointwise dominates the corresponding subtracted convex component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither ordering between decomposition-dependent lower bounds holds without an estimator comparison.

notation.meaning: majorants associated with the two decompositions

Canonical DC Outer Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cutting-plane lower approximation built from valid convex minorants of a DC objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a compact convex set \(C\), a DC objective \(f=g-h\), a tolerance \(\tau\ge0\), and an oracle producing concave majorants \(U_k\ge h\) on \(C\). Initialize a feasible incumbent \(x^0\) and \(B^0=f(x^0)\). At iteration \(k\), form \(m_k=g-U_k\) and solve
\[
L_k=\min_{x\in C,\,t}\{t:t\ge m_j(x),\ j=1,\ldots,k\}.
\]
Evaluate a feasible trial point \(x^k\), update \(B^k=\min\{B^{k-1},f(x^k)\}\), and stop when \(B^k-L_k\le\tau\). Otherwise generate \(U_{k+1}\) and repeat. The output is \(\tau\)-globally optimal whenever \(L_k\) is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method accumulates convex minorant cuts, solves their epigraph master for a lower bound, updates a feasible incumbent, and stops when the global gap meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Each oracle output \(U_k\) is concave and satisfies \(U_k\ge h\) on \(C\).
The master and trial-point subproblems are solved to the declared accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination with \(B^k-L_k\le\tau\) returns an incumbent whose objective is within \(\tau\) of the global optimum.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Outer-Approximation Algorithm for Canonical DC Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex-based polyhedral outer approximation for canonical DC programs, including approximate-optimality and infeasibility termination cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \begin{aligned}&\gamma_1=f(\bar x^1)\text{ for the best known feasible point, or }(\bar x^1,\gamma_1)=(\varnothing,+\infty),\\&P_1=\{x\in P_0\mid f(x)\le\gamma_1\},\qquad P_0\supset D.\\&x^k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in V_k}h(x).\quad h(x^k)<0\Rightarrow\begin{cases}\bar x^k\text{ is }\varepsilon\text{-approximate},&\gamma_k<+\infty,\\(CDC)\text{ is infeasible},&\gamma_k=+\infty.\end{cases}\\&\text{Otherwise choose }y^k\in[w,x^k]\text{ such that }\max\{g(y^k),h(y^k)+\varepsilon\}=0.\\&g(y^k)=0:\quad l_k(x)=\langle p^k,x-y^k\rangle,\quad p^k\in\partial g(y^k),\text{ with the incumbent retained};\\&h(y^k)=-\varepsilon:\quad \gamma_{k+1}=\min\{\gamma_k,f(y^k)\},\text{ update the incumbent as prescribed,}\\&\hspace{31mm}l_k(x)=\langle p^k,x-y^k\rangle,\quad p^k\in\partial f(y^k).\\&P_{k+1}=P_k\cap\{x\mid l_k(x)\le0\};\text{ compute }V_{k+1}\text{ and repeat.}\end{aligned}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize a polytope containing D and restrict it by the best available objective bound. At iteration k, maximize h over the current vertices. If the maximum is negative, return the incumbent as ε-approximate when one exists; otherwise declare the problem infeasible. If termination does not occur, select the prescribed point yᵏ on [w,xᵏ], form a subgradient cut from g when g(yᵏ)=0 or from f when h(yᵏ)=−ε, update the incumbent in the latter case as prescribed, intersect the polytope with the cut, recompute its vertices, and repeat.

V_k\text{ is the vertex set of }P_k
\bar x^1\text{ is the best available feasible point when one is known}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Combined Outer-Approximation and Conical-Subdivision Algorithm for Canonical DC Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithmic scheme for solving a canonical DC program using conical subdivision, LP-based screening, and outer-approximation cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an incumbent \(\bar{x}^1\) with bound \(\gamma_1=c\bar{x}^1\), or set \(\bar{x}^1=\varnothing\) and \(\gamma_1=+\infty\) if no feasible point is known; choose a polytope \(P_0\supset D\), set \(P_1=\{x\in P_0:cx\leq\gamma_1\}\), and initialize a conical partition of \(\mathbb R_+^n\). At iteration \(k\), for every current cone \(M\) with edge matrix \(U=[u^1,\ldots,u^n]\) and boundary-intersection scalars \(\theta_i\), solve \[\mu(M)=\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{t_i}{\theta_i}:Ut\in P_k,\ t\geq0\right\},\qquad \omega(M)=U\bar t(M).\] Discard cones with \(\mu(M)<1\). If none remain, return \(\bar{x}^k\) as an \(\varepsilon\)-approximate optimum when \(\gamma_k<+\infty\), and otherwise declare infeasibility. Select a remaining cone maximizing \(\mu\); if its point \(\omega^k\) belongs to \(D(\gamma^k)=\{x\in D:f(x)\leq\gamma^k\}\), return \(\omega^k\) as a global optimum. Otherwise subdivide the selected cone along the ray through \(\omega^k\). Whenever \(h(\omega(M))>-\varepsilon\) for a remaining cone, choose \(y^k\in[0,x^k]\) satisfying \(\max\{g(y^k),h(y^k)+\varepsilon\}=0\), generate the applicable OA cut, update the incumbent and bound when the cut arises from the second case, intersect \(P_k\) with the cut, update the cone family, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from the best known feasible point, or an infinite bound if none is known, a polyhedral outer set containing the domain, and a conical partition of the nonnegative orthant. At each iteration solve one screening LP per active cone, remove cones whose score is below one, and terminate with an approximate optimum or infeasibility if no cones remain. For a cone with maximum score, return its evaluation point if that point meets the incumbent-level feasibility condition; otherwise subdivide the cone. When the DC constraint residual is within the tolerance threshold, construct the appropriate outer-approximation cut, update the incumbent when a new feasible point is obtained, refine the outer polytope and cone collection, and continue.
assumptions_latex: \gamma_1=c\bar{x}^1\text{ for a known feasible incumbent, or }(\bar{x}^1,\gamma_1)=(\varnothing,+\infty).
\text{Each cone edge meets }\partial C\text{ at }\theta_i u^i\text{ and the stated screening LP is solvable.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal R_k=\varnothing\Rightarrow\begin{cases}\bar{x}^k\text{ is an }\varepsilon\text{-approximate optimum},&\gamma_k<+\infty,\\(CDC)\text{ is infeasible},&\gamma_k=+\infty,\end{cases}\qquad \omega^k\in D(\gamma^k)\Rightarrow \omega^k\text{ is globally optimal};\text{ otherwise the conical partition and OA model are refined.}

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Approximation Master Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph master combining accumulated regional or global convex minorants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_k\subseteq C\) be the current search region and let \(m_1,\ldots,m_k\) be convex functions satisfying \(m_j(x)\le f(x)\) on \(C_k\). The outer-approximation master is
\[
L_k=\begin{aligned}[t]
\min_{x,t}&\quad t\\
\text{subject to}&\quad x\in C_k,\\
&\quad t\ge m_j(x),\qquad j=1,\ldots,k.
\end{aligned}
\]
Equivalently, \(L_k=\min_{x\in C_k}\max_{j\le k}m_j(x)\). Since the pointwise maximum remains below \(f\),
\[
L_k\le\inf_{x\in C_k}f(x).
\]
Adding a valid cut cannot decrease \(L_k\) while the region remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master minimizes the epigraph of the maximum accumulated convex minorant; its value is a valid regional lower bound and increases monotonically as cuts are added.
assumptions_latex: Every \(m_j\) is convex and minorizes \(f\) on \(C_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\le\inf_{C_k}f\), and adding valid minorants cannot lower \(L_k\) for fixed \(C_k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Based Bounding Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic branch-and-bound using DC regional lower bounds and feasible incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a compact initial region \(C_0\), objective \(f=g-h\), and tolerance \(\tau\ge0\). Maintain active nodes \(R\subseteq C_0\), valid bounds \(L(R)\le\inf_{x\in R}f(x)\), and an incumbent value \(B\) from feasible evaluations. Repeatedly select an active node with smallest lower bound. If \(L(R)\ge B-\tau\), prune it; otherwise partition it into finitely many children, compute their valid lower bounds, update \(B\), and retain unpruned children. Stop when
\[
B-\min_{R\text{ active}}L(R)\le\tau,
\]
or no active node remains. Return the incumbent point and \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch-and-bound partitions the domain, computes valid regional DC lower bounds, prunes regions unable to improve the incumbent, and terminates at the prescribed global gap.
assumptions_latex: \(C_0\) is compact and every generated child family covers its parent.
Each \(L(R)\) is a valid regional lower bound.
Incumbent values arise from feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination the returned incumbent satisfies \(f(\bar x)\le\inf_{x\in C_0}f(x)+\tau\).

notation.meaning: lower bound for search region R

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Tolerance Convergence Under Uniformly Consistent Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient convergence regime for regional DC branch-and-bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let active regions cover every unresolved feasible point of a compact set \(F\). Suppose that at iteration \(k\) every active region has diameter at most \(\delta_k\), where \(\delta_k\to0\), and that functions \(\omega,\eta\) satisfy \(\omega(t),\eta(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\). For each active region \(R\), assume \[\inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x)-\omega(\operatorname{diam}R)\le L(R)\le\inf_{x\in F\cap R}f(x),\] and assume a feasible trial associated with every active region has value at most \(\inf_{F\cap R}f+\eta(\operatorname{diam}R)\). If \(L_k=\min_R L(R)\) and \(U_k\) is the incumbent value, then \[0\le U_k-L_k\le\omega(\delta_k)+\eta(\delta_k).\] Consequently, every positive absolute tolerance is certified after finitely many iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly shrinking covered regions, uniformly consistent lower bounds, and uniformly accurate feasible trials force the global branch-and-bound gap to zero and give finite epsilon termination.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is nonempty and compact, and active regions cover all unresolved feasible points.
The maximum active-region diameter \(\delta_k\) tends to zero unless the algorithm terminates.
Regional lower-bound error is bounded by \(\omega(\operatorname{diam}R)\).
Regional feasible-trial error is bounded by \(\eta(\operatorname{diam}R)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le U_k-L_k\le\omega(\delta_k)+\eta(\delta_k)\to0.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{f(x):x\in F\}\), where \(F\subseteq R_0\), and let \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Maintain active node regions \(R\subseteq R_0\), a feasible incumbent \(\hat x\in F\), and \(U=f(\hat x)\). At a node \(R\), solve an outer relaxation containing \(F\cap R\) and obtain a rigorous lower bound \(L_R\). Use only cuts valid on \(R\), and inherit such a cut at a descendant \(R'\subseteq R\) only when it remains valid there. Update \(\hat x\) and \(U\) whenever a better feasible point is found. Prune \(R\) if its relaxation is infeasible or \(L_R\ge U-\varepsilon\); otherwise replace it by children whose union contains \(F\cap R\). If no active node remains, return \(\hat x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate node relaxations, valid cuts, feasible incumbents, pruning, and coverage-preserving branching. If this process exhausts the active tree, its incumbent has absolute objective gap at most the requested tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Elementary False-Certificate Failure Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete one-dimensional witnesses for invalid cuts, overstated bounds, and incomplete child coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{x:0\le x\le1\}\), whose unique minimizer is \(0\), and suppose the incumbent is \(x=1\) with value \(U=1\). An invalid cut \(x\ge\tfrac12\) removes the minimizer. Alternatively, assigning the region containing \(0\) the invalid lower bound \(\widetilde L=1\) permits it to be pruned against \(U\). Finally, replacing \([0,1]\) only by the child \([\tfrac12,1]\) loses coverage even when every bound on that child is valid. Each alteration permits exhaustion of the represented search while the returned incumbent is not globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On minimizing x over [0,1], an invalid cut, an overstated bound, or omission of the left child can each remove the unique optimizer and permit a false exhausted-tree certificate.
assumptions_latex: The represented search is declared complete after the corrupted region accounting is exhausted.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity, Coverage, and Gap-Closure Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary specific to interactions among outer-approximation cuts, node bounds, pruning, and branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A combined cut–tree method can produce a false certificate if a cut excludes an improving feasible point, a computed node value exceeds the true node infimum, or the children fail to cover the feasible portion of their parent. With valid cuts, bounds, and coverage, certification may still fail to occur if refinement leaves a nonvanishing lower-bound error or feasible-trial error. Nonattainment alone precludes returning an exact minimizer but does not by itself preclude positive-tolerance value certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invalid cuts or bounds and lost branching coverage can make a certificate false; persistent relaxation or trial errors can prevent gap closure. Nonattainment affects exact solutions but need not prevent epsilon certification.
assumptions_latex: The method prunes nodes using relaxation lower bounds and a feasible incumbent.
A claimed global certificate accounts for all unresolved feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Sound certification requires valid cuts and bounds, preserved coverage, and sufficiently vanishing bound and trial errors.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conical branch-and-bound algorithm for BCP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm combining vertex incumbents, conical lower bounds, optional valid cuts, pruning, and omega-subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with a feasible z^0 and a vertex local minimizer \bar x with f(\bar x)\le f(z^0). Choose a vertex local minimizer x^0 satisfying f(x^0)>f(\bar x)-\varepsilon, initialize its canonical cone M_0, active collections \mathcal P=\mathcal N=\{M_0\}, and \gamma=f(\bar x). For each newly generated cone M, solve LP(D,M), obtain \mu(M) and \omega(M), and compute the valid lower bound \beta(M). If f(\omega(M))<\gamma, either add a (\gamma-\varepsilon)-valid cut and restart the local-minimizer phases, or replace the incumbent by a vertex \widehat x with f(\widehat x)\le f(\omega(M)). Delete every M with \beta(M)\ge\gamma-\varepsilon. If no cone remains, return \bar x; otherwise choose a remaining cone minimizing \beta, perform an \omega-subdivision, update the cone net, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The algorithm initializes feasible and locally minimizing vertices and a canonical cone. It computes conical lower bounds and omega points, optionally adds a valid cut or improves the incumbent, prunes cones that cannot improve the tolerance threshold, terminates when none remain, and otherwise omega-subdivides a cone with minimum lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \bar x\text{ is a vertex local minimizer with }f(\bar x)\le f(z^0)
x^0\text{ is a vertex local minimizer with }f(x^0)>f(\bar x)-\varepsilon
\beta(M)\text{ is computed by the stated valid conical lower-bounding rule}
\omega\text{-subdivision is available for each selected cone}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal R=\varnothing\implies\bar x\text{ is a global }\varepsilon\text{-optimal solution of (BCP); otherwise refine }M_*\in\arg\min_{M\in\mathcal R}\beta(M).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LP-Bounded Rectangle Branch-and-Bound Algorithm for SBCP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound procedure for the separable concave program denoted SBCP in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a feasible incumbent \bar x^0 and the active rectangle set with M_0=[c,d]. At iteration k, solve LP(D,M) for each M\in\mathcal P_k to obtain \beta(M) and a basic optimal solution \omega(M); update \bar x^k from \bar x^{k-1} and the points \omega(M). Prune every M\in\mathcal N_k satisfying \beta(M)\ge f(\bar x^k)-\varepsilon. If no rectangle remains, return \bar x^k as globally \varepsilon\text{-optimal}. Otherwise choose M_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{M\in\mathcal R_k}\beta(M), set \omega^k=\omega(M_k), select j_k by the maximum componentwise gap f_j(\omega_j^k)-\varphi_{M_k,j}(\omega_j^k), subdivide M_k through (\omega^k,j_k), replace M_k by the resulting partition, and repeat.

An empty remaining set certifies global epsilon-optimality.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal R_k=\varnothing\implies \bar x^k\text{ is a globally }\varepsilon\text{-optimal solution of (SBCP).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm as extracted; its referenced sets, cones, and linear programs are defined outside this item.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a simplex \(\bar M=\operatorname{conv}\{w^1,\ldots,w^{n+1}\}\supseteq D\) and an interior point \(w^0\in D\). Initialize \(t^0=3\bigl(\min_{h=1,\ldots,m}\|w^0-p_h\|+\max_{i,j=1,\ldots,n+1}\|w^i-w^j\|\bigr)\), \(v^0=w^0\), construct and partition the prescribed cone, and initialize the active partition and bounds. Prune cones whose upper bound cannot improve the incumbent, refine a cone with maximum remaining upper bound, and continue until no active cones remain. The extracted stopping rule reports infeasibility when the final upper value equals the initial t-value and otherwise returns the stored solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Outer-approximation algorithm for COP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A DC outer-approximation scheme over a simplex or rectangle known to contain an optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a simplex or rectangle containing an optimal solution. Initialize \(x^0\in M\) and \(\alpha_0=f(x^0)\) if \(x^0\in S\), otherwise \(\alpha_0=+\infty\). At iteration \(k\), optionally improve feasible \(x^k\) locally, retain the best incumbent \(\bar x^k\), set \(\alpha_k=f(\bar x^k)\) when it exists and \(+\infty\) otherwise, and form \(\ell_k(x)=2\langle x^k,x\rangle-\|x^k\|^2+r^2(\alpha_k,x^k)\). Solve \(\min\{t-\|x\|^2:x\in M,\ \ell_i(x)\le t,\ i=1,\ldots,k\}\) to obtain \((x^{k+1},t^{k+1})\). If \(t^{k+1}-\|x^{k+1}\|^2>0\), declare \(S=\varnothing\). If it equals zero, declare infeasibility when \(\alpha_k=+\infty\), and otherwise return \(\bar x^k\) as a global solution. If it is negative, continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The OA method successively adds affine relief cuts, solves a DC master problem over a known bounding simplex or rectangle, and uses the master value's sign to certify infeasibility, certify the incumbent's global optimality, or continue.
assumptions_latex: M\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ is a simplex or rectangle containing an optimal solution}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t^{k+1}-\|x^{k+1}\|^2>0\Rightarrow S=\varnothing;\quad t^{k+1}-\|x^{k+1}\|^2=0\Rightarrow [\alpha_k=+\infty\Rightarrow S=\varnothing,\ \alpha_k<+\infty\Rightarrow \bar x^k\text{ solves }(\mathrm{COP})];\quad t^{k+1}-\|x^{k+1}\|^2<0\Rightarrow\text{continue}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simplicial Interpolation Branch-and-Bound for Separated Nonconvexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplicial convex lower bounding and convergence when the subtracted convex term depends on a separated variable block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{G(x,y)-H(y):(x,y)\in C,\ y\in Y\}\), where \(C\) is convex, \(Y\) is a compact polytope, and \(G,H\) are convex. For a simplex \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_m\}\) in a triangulation of \(Y\), let \(\overline H_S\) be the affine vertex interpolant of \(H\). Then \(H(y)\le\overline H_S(y)\) on \(S\), so minimizing \(G(x,y)-\overline H_S(y)\) over \((x,y)\in C\), \(y\in S\), gives a convex regional lower bound. A simplicial branch-and-bound method subdivides live simplices, updates feasible incumbents, and prunes by rigorous lower bounds. Under fair exhaustive refinement with maximum live-simplex diameter tending to zero, rigorous node solution, and consistent incumbent generation, interpolation error vanishes uniformly and the incumbent–lower-bound gap converges to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Triangulate the separated variable polytope, use affine vertex overestimators to form convex node bounds, and refine exhaustively to global convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is a compact polytope admitting a finite conforming triangulation.
The relevant feasible region is nonempty and compact, and \(C\) is convex.
\(G\) and \(H\) are finite and convex on the relevant domain.
Refinement is fair and exhaustive, node bounds are rigorous, and maximum live-simplex diameter tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every simplicial node supplies a valid convex lower bound, and exhaustive vanishing-mesh refinement yields global bound-gap convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplicial Interpolation Branch-and-Bound for Separated Nonconvexity
Simplicial Methods for Separated Nonconvexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplicial lower bounding when the concave DC term depends on a separated variable block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{G(x,y)-H(y):(x,y)\in C,\ y\in Y\}\), where \(G\) and \(H\) are convex and \(Y\) is compact. Triangulate \(Y\) into simplices. For a simplex \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_m\}\), let \(\overline H_S\) be the affine interpolant satisfying \(\overline H_S(v_i)=H(v_i)\). Repeatedly subdivide an unpruned simplex, update feasible incumbents, and prune by the incumbent-gap test.

The simplicial refinement is exhaustive and its maximum diameter tends to zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rectangular Secant Branch-and-Bound for Separated Nonconvexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boxwise convex lower bounding and convergence for coordinate-separable subtracted convex terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min\{G(x,y)-\sum_{j=1}^mH_j(y_j):(x,y)\in C,\ y\in Y\}\), where \(C\) is convex, \(Y\) is a compact box, and \(G,H_j\) are convex. On \(R=\prod_j[a_j,b_j]\subseteq Y\), let \(s_{j,R}\) be the endpoint secant of \(H_j\). Then \(H_j(t)\le s_{j,R}(t)\), and minimizing
\[G(x,y)-\sum_j s_{j,R}(y_j)\]
over \((x,y)\in C\), \(y\in R\), gives a convex regional lower-bounding problem. A rectangular branch-and-bound method bisects live boxes, updates feasible incumbents, and safely prunes boxes whose rigorous lower bounds cannot improve the incumbent. If selection and branching are exhaustive, live-box widths tend to zero, node problems are bounded rigorously, and feasible incumbents are generated consistently, the aggregate secant error vanishes uniformly and the usual incumbent–lower-bound test yields global convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinatewise secants create convex box lower bounds for a separated subtracted term; exhaustive shrinking-box branch-and-bound converges globally.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and the relevant feasible region is nonempty and compact.
Each \(H_j\) is finite and convex on its coordinate interval.
Branching and selection are exhaustive, node bounds are rigorous, and maximum live-box width tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every node value is a valid lower bound, secant error vanishes under refinement, and the global bound gap converges to zero under the stated search conditions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rectangular branch-and-bound bounds for separable concave network costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chord lower bounds, convergence, and the stated integral-data finiteness regime for rectangular subdivision of (SCP).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(g(y)=\sum_{i=1}^r g_i(y_i)\) is concave and separable. For \(M=[a,b]\), let \(l_{i,M}\) be the affine chord agreeing with \(g_i\) at \(a_i\) and \(b_i\), and set \(l_M(y)=\sum_{i=1}^r l_{i,M}(y_i)\). For the integral transportation case, if all data and the initial rectangle vertices are integral, the generated subrectangles have integral vertices and the algorithm is finite.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cellwise Lower Models from Noncanonical DC Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity, strengthening order, and tractability boundary for lower models induced by a chosen DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(z)=G(z)-H(Az)\) on \(Z_R\), where \(G\) and \(H\) are convex and \(AZ_R\subseteq R\). If \(\overline H_R\) satisfies \(H(y)\le\overline H_R(y)\) on \(R\), then
\[m_R(z)=G(z)-\overline H_R(Az)\le f(z)\quad(z\in Z_R),\]
so any rigorous lower bound on \(\inf_{Z_R}m_R\) is a valid regional lower bound. If two valid overestimators satisfy \(\overline H_R^{(1)}\le\overline H_R^{(0)}\), then \(m_R^{(1)}\ge m_R^{(0)}\). The subproblem is convex when \(\overline H_R\circ A\) is concave, in particular when \(\overline H_R\) is affine; convexity of \(\overline H_R\) alone does not provide this tractability guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any valid overestimator of the subtracted component gives a lower model, smaller overestimators strengthen it, and convex tractability requires a concave—typically affine—overestimator rather than merely a convex one.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) and \(H\) are convex on their relevant domains.
The lower-model infimum is solved or bounded rigorously.
Convex-subproblem claims additionally require \(\overline H_R\circ A\) to be concave.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is lower-valid under pointwise overestimation and convexly tractable under the stated curvature condition.

Noncanonical DC Outer Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer relaxation based on a chosen, noncanonical DC decomposition over partition cells.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(z)=G(z)-H(Az)\) on a compact convex set \(Z\), with \(G\) and \(H\) convex. For a cell \(R\) containing \(AZ_R:=\{Az:z\in Z_R\}\), choose a convexly tractable overestimator \(\overline H_R\) satisfying \(H(y)\le\overline H_R(y)\) for every \(y\in R\). Then
\[
L_R:=\inf_{z\in Z_R}\bigl(G(z)-\overline H_R(Az)\bigr)\le \inf_{z\in Z_R}f(z).
\]
Thus any selected DC decomposition, not necessarily canonical, induces an outer lower model. Refining \(R\), adding valid cuts, or tightening \(\overline H_R\) strengthens the bound while preserving validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any valid overestimator of the subtracted convex component yields a lower outer model; its strength depends on both the chosen DC decomposition and cellwise approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) and \(H\) are convex on their relevant domains.
The lower-model optimization is solved with a rigorous bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed value \(L_R\) is a valid node lower bound for the original DC objective.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Outer-approximation algorithm for (NCP)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral outer approximation using an incumbent level, maximization over the current polytope, projection, and subgradient cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the best feasible point $\bar x$ and $\gamma=f(\bar x)$, taking $\bar x=\varnothing$ and $\gamma=\alpha$ if none is known, and choose a polytope $P_1\supset\{x:f(x)\leq\gamma\}\cap\operatorname{cone}(\mathbb R^n\setminus\operatorname{int}C)$. At iteration $k$, terminate with $\bar x$ solving (NCP) if $\bar x\in\arg\min\{f(x):x\in P_k\}$. Otherwise choose $z^k\in\arg\max\{f(x):x\in P_k\}$ and compute $\pi(z^k)$. If $\pi(z^k)$ exists and $f(\pi(z^k))<\gamma$, set $\bar x=\pi(z^k)$ and $\gamma=f(\pi(z^k))$. Choose $y^k\in[0,z^k]\cap\{x:f(x)=\gamma\}$ and $p^k\in\partial f(y^k)$, set $P_{k+1}=P_k\cap\{x:\langle p^k,x-y^k\rangle\leq0\}$, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from the best known feasible point and a polytope containing the specified incumbent-level portion of the noncanonical domain. If the incumbent minimizes the objective over the current polytope, return it as a solution. Otherwise maximize the objective over the polytope, project the maximizer when possible, and adopt any improving projected point. At the incumbent level on the segment from zero to the maximizer, form a subgradient halfspace, intersect it with the current polytope, and repeat.
assumptions_latex: \gamma=f(\bar x)\text{ for the best known feasible }\bar x,\text{ or }(\bar x,\gamma)=(\varnothing,\alpha)\text{ if none is known}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\in\arg\min\{f(x):x\in P_k\}\Rightarrow\bar x\text{ solves (NCP)};\qquad P_{k+1}=P_k\cap\{x:\langle p^k,x-y^k\rangle\leq0\}\text{ otherwise}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral outer approximation using visible feasible points and subgradient cuts, under the section's standing assumptions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Outer-Approximation Algorithm for DC Design Centering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Successive affine underestimation of the convex auxiliary function over a simplex containing the design set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose an \(n\)-simplex \(Z_0\supset S\), a point \(x^0\in S\), and set \(y^0=x^0\). For \(k\ge1\), define
\[
f_k(x)=x^TAx-\max_{0\le i<k}\left\{\left\langle2Ay^i,x-x^i\right\rangle+g(x^i)\right\},
\]
and solve
\[
\max_{x\in Z_0}f_k(x)
\]
to obtain \(x^k\). If \(x^k\in S\), solve
\[
\max_{y\notin\operatorname{int}S}\left\{2(x^k)^TAy-y^TAy\right\}
\]
to obtain \(y^k\) and \(g(x^k)\). Stop if
\[
f_k(x^k)=(x^k)^TAx^k-g(x^k);
\]
otherwise increment \(k\). If \(x^k\notin S\), set \(y^k=x^k\), increment \(k\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The algorithm maximizes models built from accumulated affine supports of g over a containing simplex. Feasible trial points trigger an auxiliary maximization and exactness test; infeasible trial points become new support points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_k(x^k)=(x^k)^TAx^k-g(x^k)\Rightarrow\text{the algorithm stops and returns }x^k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Successive Incumbent-Transcending Level Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-tolerance global level-feasibility search, its stopping certificate, and its finite-success bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\ne\varnothing\), let \(f=g-h\) be bounded below on \(F\), choose \(x^0\in F\), and set \(U_0=f(x^0)\). For fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), at iteration \(k\) globally find an \(x\in F\) satisfying \(f(x)<U_k-\varepsilon\), or certify that none exists. A witness becomes the next incumbent. Infeasibility implies \(U_k\le\inf_F f+\varepsilon\). If \(f_*=\inf_F f\), every successful iteration decreases the incumbent by more than \(\varepsilon\), so the number \(N\) of successful iterations satisfies \(N<(U_0-f_*)/\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly search globally below the incumbent by a fixed margin; a witness improves it, while infeasibility certifies epsilon-global optimality and forces finite termination.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is nonempty and \(f\) is bounded below on \(F\).
Every strict level-feasibility problem is solved globally or certified infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method has finitely many successful iterations and terminates with \(U_k\le\inf_F f+\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Successive Incumbent-Transcending Level Search
Successive Incumbent-Transcending Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact level-feasibility scheme that repeatedly seeks a point improving the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f=g-h\) on a compact feasible set \(F\), choose a feasible \(x^0\), set \(U_0=f(x^0)\), and fix \(\varepsilon>0\). At iteration \(k\), globally solve or certify infeasibility of the level problem
\[
\text{find }x\in F\text{ such that }g(x)-h(x)<U_k-\varepsilon.
\]
If infeasible, return \(x^k\); it is \(\varepsilon\)-globally optimal. If a feasible \(x^{k+1}\) is found, set \(U_{k+1}=f(x^{k+1})\) and repeat. With an exact feasibility oracle, every successful iteration decreases the incumbent by more than \(\varepsilon\), so boundedness below implies finitely many successful iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve a global level-feasibility problem below the incumbent. A witness improves the incumbent; infeasibility certifies that no point improves it by the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is nonempty and \(f\) is bounded below on \(F\).
Each level-feasibility problem is solved or certified infeasible globally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination by infeasibility yields \(f(x^k)\le \inf_{x\in F}f(x)+\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Outer-Safe Treatment of Hard DC Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Containment and penalty conditions needed to preserve hard DC constraints during global bounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For node \(R\) and constraints \(c_i(x)=g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le0\), suppose \(\underline c_{i,R}(x)\le c_i(x)\) for every \(x\in R\). Then
\[\{x\in R:c_i(x)\le0\ \forall i\}\subseteq\{x\in R:\underline c_{i,R}(x)\le0\ \forall i\}.\]
Certified infeasibility of the relaxed system therefore certifies infeasibility of the original node. Replacing hard constraints by a finite penalty is equivalent only under a problem-specific exact-penalty theorem. Indeed, for any fixed \(\rho<\infty\), minimizing \(- (\rho+1)|x|+\rho|x|\) on \([-1,1]\) as a penalty replacement for the hard constraint \(x=0\) yields minimizers \(x=\pm1\), whereas the constrained feasible set is \(\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard DC constraints must remain outer-safe in node relaxations; an arbitrary finite penalty is not an exact replacement.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i\) and \(h_i\) is convex on the node domain.
Node rejection uses certified infeasibility of a relaxation containing the original feasible set.
Any asserted penalty replacement has an independently justified exact-penalty threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relaxation infeasibility is safe under outer containment, while finite penalization is unsafe without exactness hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Safe Treatment of Hard DC Constraints
Hard-Constraint DC Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for globally bounding DC problems with constraints that cannot be relaxed by unsafe penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For constraints \(c_i(x)=g_i(x)-h_i(x)\le0\), a node \(R\) is hard-constraint safe when its relaxation uses functions \(\underline c_{i,R}\) satisfying
\[
\underline c_{i,R}(x)\le c_i(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in R,
\]
and declares node infeasibility only after certifying that no \(x\in R\) satisfies all relaxed inequalities \(\underline c_{i,R}(x)\le0\). Consequently, the relaxed feasible set contains the original feasible set within \(R\). A finite penalty substitution is not equivalent unless an independently justified exact-penalty threshold is available; otherwise pruning must retain the explicit hard constraints through valid outer relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard DC constraints require outer-feasible node relaxations. An arbitrary finite penalty cannot replace them without a proven exact-penalty threshold.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i\) and \(h_i\) is convex on the node domain.
Node rejection is based on certified relaxation infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible point of the original constrained problem remains feasible for the node relaxation and therefore cannot be removed solely by relaxed infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Paired-Inequality Representation of a DC Equality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact treatment of a DC equality and the failure boundaries of one-sided or tolerance-based replacements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q,r:X\to\mathbb R\) be finite convex functions. Then
\[q(x)-r(x)=0\iff q(x)-r(x)\le0\ \text{and}\ r(x)-q(x)\le0.\]
Thus an inequality-based DC global method handles the equality exactly only when it retains both orientations. Retaining one orientation is generally a strict relaxation: for \(q(x)=0\), \(r(x)=x\), and \(X=[0,1]\), the inequality \(q-r\le0\) admits every \(x\in X\), whereas the equality admits only \(x=0\). Replacing equality by \(|q-r|\le\tau\) with \(\tau>0\) defines tolerance feasibility and need not preserve the exact feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DC equality is exactly two opposing DC inequalities; one-sided enforcement or a positive residual tolerance generally enlarges the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) and \(r\) are finite convex functions on \(X\).
All relations are interpreted pointwise on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact equality enforcement requires both inequality orientations and zero residual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Paired-Inequality Representation of a DC Equality
DC Equality-Constraint Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conversion of a DC equality into two DC inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q,r:X\to\mathbb R\) be convex on a convex domain \(X\). The DC equality
\[
q(x)-r(x)=0
\]
is equivalent to the pair
\[
q(x)-r(x)\le0,\qquad r(x)-q(x)\le0.
\]
Both inequalities are DC constraints. Hence a global method for DC inequalities may enforce the equality by retaining both directions and constructing valid outer relaxations for each. Enforcing only one direction yields a strict relaxation in general. Likewise, replacing the pair by \(\lvert q(x)-r(x)\rvert\le\tau\) changes the feasible set unless \(\tau=0\), although positive \(\tau\) may define an explicit feasibility tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DC equality is exactly two opposing DC inequalities. Both must be retained; one direction or a positive residual tolerance changes the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) and \(r\) are finite convex functions on \(X\).
Equality and inequalities are interpreted pointwise over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in X\), \(q(x)-r(x)=0\) if and only if both displayed DC inequalities hold.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Kernel-Guided Reduction to an Undominated DC Matrix
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative rank-one reduction of a valid matrix DC decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start with \(B\in\mathbb S^n\) such that \(B\succeq0\) and \(B-A\succeq0\). Compute \(\ker(B)\) and \(\ker(B-A)\). If their span is \(\mathbb R^n\), return \(B\). Otherwise choose \(0\ne y\in(\ker(B)+\ker(B-A))^\perp\), set \(B\leftarrow B-\gamma yy^T\), where \(\gamma=\max\{\varepsilon:B-\varepsilon yy^T\succeq0,\ B-\varepsilon yy^T-A\succeq0\}\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly choose a direction orthogonal to both current kernels and subtract the largest feasible positive-semidefinite rank-one term. Stop when the two kernels span the whole space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Return }B\text{ when }\ker(B)+\ker(B-A)=\mathbb R^n

children.title: DC Decomposition Nonuniqueness
children.top_down_role: Multiplicity of valid DC decompositions for the same model.

knowledge_statements.title: DC Decomposition Nonuniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic nonuniqueness of convex-minus-convex representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(f=g-h\) on a convex set \(X\), where \(g\) and \(h\) are convex. For every convex function \(\psi:X\to\mathbb R\),
\[
f=(g+\psi)-(h+\psi),
\]
and both new components are convex. Thus, whenever one DC decomposition exists, infinitely many generally distinct decompositions exist, for example by taking \(\psi(x)=\alpha\lVert x\rVert^2\) with any \(\alpha\ge0\) in a Euclidean space. The represented objective and its minimizers are unchanged, but relaxations that approximate the subtracted component may change because they act on \(h+\psi\), not directly on \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding the same convex function to both DC components preserves the objective, creating infinitely many decompositions whose induced global relaxations may differ.
assumptions_latex: \(g\), \(h\), and \(\psi\) are finite convex functions on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((g+\psi,h+\psi)\) is another DC decomposition of exactly the same function \(f\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Dominance Is Sufficient but Not Necessary for Better Optimized Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinction between pointwise error ranking and solved cell-bound ranking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a common objective \(f\) on a cell \(R\), models \(m_i=f-e_i\) with \(e_i\ge0\) satisfy \(e_1\le e_2\Rightarrow m_1\ge m_2\Rightarrow\inf_Rm_1\ge\inf_Rm_2\). The converse fails. For \(f\equiv0\) on \([0,1]\), take \(e_1(x)=x\) and \(e_2(x)=2(1-x)\). The errors cross, so neither model dominates pointwise, but \[\inf_{[0,1]}(-e_1)=-1>-2=\inf_{[0,1]}(-e_2).\] Thus pointwise error dominance is a strong sufficient criterion, while optimized lower-bound value is a weaker comparison criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise smaller error guarantees a better bound, but crossing errors can still yield a strict ordering of optimized lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: Both models underestimate the same objective on the same nonempty cell.
The displayed example uses nonnegative bounded errors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pointwise error dominance implies bound dominance but is not necessary for it.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Dominance Is Sufficient but Not Necessary for Better Optimized Bounds
DC Decomposition Quality Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cellwise dominance criterion for decomposition quality in outer lower bounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a decomposition \(f=g-h\) and a partition cell \(R\), let \(\overline h_R\ge h\) be the overestimator used by the lower model and define its error by
\[
e_R(x):=\overline h_R(x)-h(x)\ge0.
\]
The induced model equals \(g(x)-\overline h_R(x)=f(x)-e_R(x)\). Given two decompositions and their prescribed overestimator constructions, decomposition \(1\) dominates decomposition \(2\) on \(R\) when \(e_R^{(1)}(x)\le e_R^{(2)}(x)\) for every \(x\in R\). Useful secondary criteria are inexpensive construction, tractable lower-model minimization, and errors converging uniformly to zero as \(\operatorname{diam}(R)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decomposition is bound-superior on a cell when its overestimation error is pointwise smaller, subject also to tractable construction and vanishing error under refinement.
assumptions_latex: Both decompositions represent the same objective on \(R\).
Each selected overestimator is valid throughout \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pointwise error dominance implies a pointwise tighter lower model and hence a no-worse node lower bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent DC Decompositions Can Give Unequal Cell Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete realization of decomposition-sensitive lower bounds under affine majorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R=[0,1]\) and \(f\equiv0\). The decomposition \(f=0-0\), with exact overestimator \(0\), gives lower model \(m_1=0\) and bound \(L_1=0\). The equivalent decomposition \(f=x^2-x^2\), with the affine chord \(\overline h(x)=x\ge x^2\) on \(R\), gives \[m_2(x)=x^2-x\quad\text{and}\quad L_2=\min_{x\in R}(x^2-x)=-\tfrac14.\] Thus the represented objective is unchanged while the rigorous cell lower bound changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two equivalent decompositions of the zero function yield lower bounds zero and minus one quarter under their specified valid majorants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_1=0>-\tfrac14=L_2\) although both decompositions represent \(f\equiv0\).

notation.meaning: affine upper estimator of the subtracted convex component
cell lower bound from decomposition i

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent DC Decompositions Can Give Unequal Cell Bounds
Bound Sensitivity to Decomposition Choice
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative dependence of cell lower bounds on DC decomposition error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let two DC decompositions of the same objective induce valid cell models \(m_i(x)=f(x)-e_i(x)\) on a nonempty cell \(R\), where \(e_i(x)\ge0\), and let \(L_i=\inf_{x\in R}m_i(x)\). Then
\[
|L_1-L_2|\le \sup_{x\in R}|e_1(x)-e_2(x)|.
\]
Moreover, if \(e_1(x)\le e_2(x)\) throughout \(R\), then \(m_1(x)\ge m_2(x)\) throughout \(R\) and consequently \(L_1\ge L_2\). Thus algebraically equivalent DC decompositions can produce unequal rigorous lower bounds solely through unequal approximation errors in their subtracted convex components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower bounds from equivalent DC decompositions can differ by at most the uniform difference of their relaxation errors; pointwise smaller error always gives a stronger bound.
assumptions_latex: The two decompositions represent the same finite objective \(f\) on \(R\).
Both error functions are bounded and nonnegative on \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed sensitivity inequality and the stated monotonic ordering of \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) hold.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Crossing Node Bounds Give No Pruning Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure of search-effort ordering without uniform dominance on a common potential tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a common potential partition tree with two unresolved nodes \(A,B\), incumbent \(U=0\), tolerance \(\varepsilon=0\), and regional optima equal to \(0\). Suppose two valid decomposition-induced bound systems satisfy \[(L_A^{(1)},L_B^{(1)})=(0,-1),\qquad (L_A^{(2)},L_B^{(2)})=(-1,0).\] Under the bound test \(L_R^{(i)}\ge U\), method \(1\) prunes \(A\) but not \(B\), whereas method \(2\) prunes \(B\) but not \(A\). Thus crossing valid bounds imply neither inclusion of pruned-node sets nor a decomposition-independent ordering of generated descendants or search effort.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When decomposition-induced bounds cross across nodes, each decomposition can prune a node that the other cannot, so neither search dominates.
assumptions_latex: The comparison uses one common potential tree and common incumbent and tolerance.
All displayed bounds are valid for their regional optima.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither method's bound-pruned node set contains the other's.

notation.meaning: bound on potential node R under decomposition i

knowledge_statements.title: Crossing Node Bounds Give No Pruning Dominance
Search Sensitivity to Decomposition Choice
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of decomposition-induced bound dominance on a fixed branching search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Run two branch-and-bound searches on the same partition tree, with the same incumbent \(U\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\), and node-selection rules, but with lower bounds \(L_R^{(1)}\) and \(L_R^{(2)}\) induced by different DC decompositions. If \(L_R^{(1)}\ge L_R^{(2)}\) for every generated node \(R\), then every node pruned by \(L_R^{(2)}\ge U-\varepsilon\) is also pruned by method \(1\). Hence method \(1\) explores no additional node solely because of the bound test. Without uniform bound dominance, errors may cross between cells, so neither decomposition has a decomposition-independent ordering in explored-node count or search effort.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly stronger bounds cannot worsen pruning on a fixed tree, but crossing cellwise errors can reverse which decomposition searches fewer nodes.
assumptions_latex: Both searches use the same tree, incumbents, tolerance, and non-bound decisions.
All compared node lower bounds are rigorous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform nodewise dominance transfers directly to pruning dominance; absent it, no general search-effort ordering follows.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\), where \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, closed, and noncompact, and \(f=g-h\) on \(C\) for finite convex functions \(g,h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\). These assumptions alone imply neither a finite optimal value nor attainment: for \(C=\mathbb{R}\) and the affine DC function \(f(x)=-x\), one has \(\inf_{x\in C}f(x)=-\infty\). A sufficient additional condition is that \(f\) be level-bounded on \(C\), meaning that for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\), the sublevel set \(\{x\in C:f(x)\leq\alpha\}\) is compact. Because \(f\) is continuous and \(C\) is nonempty, this condition yields a finite attained minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closedness of a noncompact DC feasible region does not prevent escape to infinity. If the finite DC objective is level-bounded on the region, its minimum is finite and attained.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Coercivity Characterization of Level-Boundedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent sequential formulation of level-boundedness on a closed noncompact feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be continuous. Then all sublevel sets \(\{x\in C:f(x)\le\alpha\}\) are compact if and only if every sequence \((x_k)\subset C\) with \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\) satisfies \(f(x_k)\to+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous objective on a closed finite-dimensional region, level-boundedness is equivalent to coercivity along every feasible sequence escaping to infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is level-bounded on }C\iff\bigl(\|x_k\|\to\infty,\ x_k\in C\bigr)\Rightarrow f(x_k)\to+\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Coercivity Characterization of Level-Boundedness

children.title: Weak DC Minorants
children.top_down_role: Minorant regimes that provide limited global information.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_D\text{ is }\varepsilon\text{-weak}\iff f_D^*-\beta_D\geq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: lower bound induced by the minorant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative definition of weakness for a valid regional minorant used in DC optimization.

source_refs.locator: 4.7 Convex Minorants of a DC Function p. 117
11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\), and let \(m_D:D\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\) satisfy \(m_D(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in D\). Write \(f_D^*=\inf_{x\in D}f(x)\) and \(\beta_D=\inf_{x\in D}m_D(x)\). For \(\varepsilon>0\), the minorant is called \(\varepsilon\)-weak on \(D\) when \(f_D^*\) is finite and \(f_D^*-\beta_D\geq\varepsilon\), with the difference interpreted as \(+\infty\) if \(\beta_D=-\infty\). It remains valid but provides a lower bound separated from the true regional optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid regional minorant is called epsilon-weak when its infimum lies at least epsilon below the finite true regional optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak DC Minorants

source_witnesses.locator: 4.7 Convex Minorants of a DC Function p. 117
11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Large Pointwise Error Need Not Produce a Weak Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the converse from large uniform model error to a poor optimized lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(M>0\), let \(D=[0,1]\), \(f(x)=Mx\), and \(m_D(x)=0\). Then \(m_D\le f\), \[\sup_{x\in D}(f(x)-m_D(x))=M,\] but \(f_D^*=\beta_D=0\). Thus arbitrarily large error away from all minimizers need not create a positive regional lower-bound gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minorant can have arbitrarily large error away from the optimum while still giving the exact regional lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_D(f-m_D)=M\) while \(f_D^*-\beta_D=0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Large Pointwise Error Need Not Produce a Weak Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minorant Error Bounds for Regional Weakness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relation between pointwise minorant error and the optimized regional bound gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\ne\varnothing\), let \(m_D\le f\) on \(D\), and define \(e=f-m_D\ge0\), \(f_D^*=\inf_Df\), and \(\beta_D=\inf_Dm_D\). If \(f_D^*\in\mathbb R\) and \(E:=\sup_De<\infty\), then \[0\le f_D^*-\beta_D\le E.\] If \(f\) attains its minimum at \(x^*\in D\), then \[f_D^*-\beta_D\ge e(x^*).\] Thus uniform error below \(\varepsilon\) rules out \(\varepsilon\)-weakness, while error at least \(\varepsilon\) at a regional minimizer guarantees it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regional bound gap is at most the worst pointwise minorant error and, when a minimizer exists, at least the error at that minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le f_D^*-\beta_D\le\sup_D(f-m_D)\), and \(f_D^*-\beta_D\ge f(x^*)-m_D(x^*)\) at an attained minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Minorant Error Bounds for Regional Weakness

children.title: Degenerate Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower-bound regimes with negligible regional discrimination.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent DC decompositions can make separate-term bounds arbitrarily poor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M>0\), minimize \(f_M(x)=0\) over \(D=[-1,1]\) using the DC decomposition \(f_M=g_M-h_M\), where \(g_M(x)=Mx^2\) and \(h_M(x)=Mx^2\). The separate-term lower bound is valid and equals \[B_M=\inf_{x\in D}g_M(x)-\sup_{x\in D}h_M(x)=0-M=-M.\] Nevertheless, \(f_M^*=0\) for every \(M\). Hence \(f_M^*-B_M=M\to\infty\), although the represented objective and feasible region do not change. A lower-bounding rule that ignores cancellation between DC components can therefore degenerate solely because of decomposition scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling two cancelling convex components leaves the objective unchanged but drives a separate-term lower bound to negative infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_M^*-B_M=M\to\infty\) as \(M\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: scaled convex components of the DC decomposition
