children.title: Persistent Bound Gaps
children.top_down_role: Search regimes characterized by weak separation between incumbent values and lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Bound Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonvanishing global relaxation error under repeated refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*=\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\in\mathbb{R}\). At iteration \(k\), let \(\mathcal P_k\) be a finite cover of \(C\), and let each \(B_k(D)\) satisfy \(B_k(D)\leq\inf_{x\in D}f(x)\). Define \(L_k=\min_{D\in\mathcal P_k}B_k(D)\). The bounding scheme has a persistent bound gap when \[\liminf_{k\to\infty}(f^*-L_k)>0.\] This condition may hold even when the maximum diameter of regions in \(\mathcal P_k\) tends to zero; geometric refinement alone does not ensure convergence unless the regional minorants are asymptotically exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound gap is persistent when valid global lower bounds remain uniformly below the optimum despite indefinitely fine regional refinement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}(f^*-L_k)>0\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound on region D
global lower bound at iteration k

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

source_witnesses.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Limsup Characterization of a Persistent Bound Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent asymptotic formulations for valid global lower-bound sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*\in\mathbb R\) and \(L_k\le f^*\) for every \(k\). Then \[\liminf_{k\to\infty}(f^*-L_k)=f^*-\limsup_{k\to\infty}L_k.\] Hence the gap is persistent exactly when \(\limsup_k L_k<f^*\). If \((L_k)\) is nondecreasing, then \(L_k\to L_\infty:=\sup_kL_k\le f^*\), and persistence is equivalent to \(L_\infty<f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistence means that the upper asymptotic limit of the lower bounds stays strictly below the optimum; for monotone bounds this is strict separation of their limit from the optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\liminf_k(f^*-L_k)>0\iff\limsup_kL_k<f^*\), with the stated monotone specialization.

notation.meaning: limit of a nondecreasing lower-bound sequence

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Limsup Characterization of a Persistent Bound Gap

children.title: Bound-Driven Search Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Failure modes caused by repeatedly uninformative regional bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Driven Search Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stagnation caused by repeatedly selecting a spuriously promising region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization search that at iteration \(k\) selects a region \(D_k\) attaining the smallest valid bound \(L_k=B_k(D_k)\), while \(U_k\) is the best feasible objective value found. If some \(\delta>0\) satisfies \(L_k\leq f^*-\delta\) for all sufficiently large \(k\), then the certified gap obeys \(U_k-L_k\geq\delta\) because \(U_k\geq f^*\). Consequently, no stopping rule requiring \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\) with \(0<\varepsilon<\delta\) can terminate, even if \(U_k\to f^*\). Persistent underestimation therefore causes bound-driven certification stagnation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the selected lower bound stays falsely low, the certified gap cannot close, even when incumbent values converge to the true optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k-L_k\geq\delta\) eventually, so tolerance \(\varepsilon<\delta\) cannot be certified.

source_refs.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

source_witnesses.locator: 11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Best-Bound Starvation from a Persistently Low Valid Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A valid but nonconvergent bound can make pure best-bound selection ignore a region containing the global optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the feasible set be \(D=A\cup B\) with \(A\cap B=\varnothing\), let \(f(x)=1\) for \(x\in A\) and \(f(x)=0\) for \(x\in B\), and suppose an incumbent of value \(U_0=1\) is available. Assign \(B\) the exact bound \(L(B)=0\). Suppose refinement of the selected region in \(A\) always leaves at least one descendant \(A_k\) with valid bound \(L(A_k)=-1\), and processing such descendants produces only feasible values equal to \(1\). A pure best-bound rule always has an \(A_k\) with bound below \(L(B)\), so \(B\) need never be processed and \(U_k=1>f^*=0\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistently lower valid bounds on one branch can starve an unprocessed branch containing the global optimizer.
assumptions_latex: After each selected refinement in \(A\), at least one live descendant has valid bound \(-1\).
Selection always chooses a smallest-bound node without a fairness override.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U_k=1>f^*=0\) for every \(k\), and \(B\) need never be processed.

notation.meaning: a succession of misleading descendants in A

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Bound Starvation from a Persistently Low Valid Bound

children.title: DC Representation Universality
children.top_down_role: Breadth of nonconvex models admitting DC representations.

knowledge_statements.title: DC Representation Universality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic DC representation for smooth functions on compact convex domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and suppose \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(C\). Set \(\mu=\min_{x\in C}\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2 f(x))\), which is finite, and choose \(\rho\geq\max\{0,-\mu\}\). Then \[f(x)=\left(f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x\rVert^2\right)-\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x\rVert^2\quad(x\in C).\] Both displayed components are convex on \(C\). Thus every such smooth objective admits a DC representation on the compact domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every twice continuously differentiable function on a compact convex set becomes DC after adding and subtracting a sufficiently curved quadratic.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^2(U)\) for an open neighborhood \(U\supseteq C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f=g-h\) on \(C\), where \(g=f+\rho\lVert\cdot\rVert^2/2\) and \(h=\rho\lVert\cdot\rVert^2/2\) are convex.

source_refs.locator: 4.7 Convex Minorants of a DC Function p. 117
2.2 Convex and Concave Functions p. 35

source_witnesses.locator: 4.7 Convex Minorants of a DC Function p. 117

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local-Lipschitz Boundary of Finite DC Representability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary interior regularity of finite convex-minus-convex representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex and suppose \(f=g-h\) on \(C\), where \(g,h:C\to\mathbb R\) are finite convex functions. Then \(g\), \(h\), and hence \(f\), are locally Lipschitz on \(\operatorname{ri}C\). Therefore not every finite continuous function on a compact convex set is DC. In particular, \[f(x)=\sqrt{|x|}\quad(x\in[-1,1])\] is continuous but not locally Lipschitz at the relative-interior point \(0\), so it is not the difference of two finite convex functions on that interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite DC functions are locally Lipschitz in the relative interior; square-root of absolute value is therefore not DC on an interval.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are finite convex functions on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f=g-h\) is locally Lipschitz on \(\operatorname{ri}C\), and \(x\mapsto\sqrt{|x|}\) is not DC on \([-1,1]\).
knowledge_statements.title: Local-Lipschitz Boundary of Finite DC Representability

children.title: Worst-Case DC Complexity
children.top_down_role: Worst-case computational difficulty within broadly expressive DC families.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: NP-Completeness of Concave-Quadratic Box Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case hardness already present in rational concave-quadratic minimization over a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph with nonnegative integer edge weights and weighted Laplacian \(L\), \(x^{\mathsf T}Lx=4w(\delta(S_x))\) at every \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\), where \(S_x=\{i:x_i=1\}\). Since the convex function \(x\mapsto x^{\mathsf T}Lx\) attains a maximum over \([-1,1]^n\) at a vertex, deciding whether \[\min_{x\in[-1,1]^n}-x^{\mathsf T}Lx\le -4K\] is equivalent to deciding whether the graph has a cut of weight at least \(K\). The decision problem is therefore NP-complete under binary encoding, and exact minimization is NP-hard. Its objective is concave quadratic and hence DC.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted Max-Cut is equivalent to minimizing a rational concave quadratic over a box, making this restricted DC decision problem NP-complete and exact DC minimization NP-hard.
assumptions_latex: Edge weights and \(K\) are nonnegative integers encoded in binary.
Complexity is measured in the deterministic Turing model.
The standard Laplacian convention \(x^{\mathsf T}Lx=\sum_{\{i,j\}}w_{ij}(x_i-x_j)^2\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Concave-quadratic box minimization is NP-hard, and its threshold decision form is NP-complete.}

notation.meaning: cut shore encoded by a sign vector

knowledge_statements.title: NP-Completeness of Concave-Quadratic Box Minimization
Worst-Case DC Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: NP-hardness already within concave quadratic box minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a graph with nonnegative rational edge weights, let \(L\) be its weighted Laplacian. The convex quadratic \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Lx\) attains its maximum over \([-1,1]^n\) at a vertex in \(\{-1,1\}^n\), and its vertex values encode weighted cuts up to a fixed factor. Therefore deciding whether \[\min_{x\in[-1,1]^n}-x^{\mathsf T}Lx\leq-T\] is NP-hard under the standard binary encoding. The objective is concave quadratic and hence DC. Consequently, general rationally encoded DC minimization admits no polynomial-time exact algorithm unless \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact DC minimization is NP-hard even for a concave quadratic objective over a box, by reduction from weighted Max-Cut.
assumptions_latex: Graph weights and threshold \(T\) are rational and binary encoded.
Computation is measured in the deterministic Turing model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Exact box-constrained DC minimization is NP-hard.}\)

notation.meaning: decision threshold after the fixed cut-value scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted-Max-Cut reduction is mathematically plausible and the complexity-bound content kind fits, but no source is cited. An authoritative complexity locator is required for the NP-hardness formulation, encoding assumptions, and threshold scaling before this candidate can be accepted.

children.title: Expressiveness–Tractability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Structural boundary between representational generality and exploitable tractability.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: NP-Hard Concave-Quadratic Subclass of DC Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete hardness witness showing that DC syntax alone does not imply tractability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a weighted graph with nonnegative rational edge weights and Laplacian \(L\succeq0\). The quadratic \(q(x)=-x^TLx\) is concave and therefore DC, for example \(q=0-x^TLx\). A concave function attains a minimum over the box \([0,1]^n\) at a vertex, so \[\min_{x\in[0,1]^n}-x^TLx=-\max_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}x^TLx.\] The right-hand maximization is the weighted Max-Cut problem up to its conventional constant factor. Consequently, exact minimization of a concave quadratic over a rational box, and hence unrestricted exact DC minimization, is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Concave quadratic box minimization contains weighted Max-Cut, so unrestricted exact DC minimization is NP-hard despite the compact DC representation.
assumptions_latex: The graph has nonnegative rational edge weights encoded in binary.
Complexity concerns exact global optimization in the deterministic Turing model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact minimization of DC functions over rational boxes is NP-hard, already for concave quadratics.
knowledge_statements.title: NP-Hard Concave-Quadratic Subclass of DC Minimization
Expressiveness–Tractability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: DC representability does not imply global computational tractability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The DC class contains the convex subclass obtained by taking \(h=0\), but it also contains every concave quadratic \(f=-h\) with convex quadratic \(h\). Convex minimization admits polynomial-time methods under standard rational-data or oracle assumptions, whereas exact minimization of concave quadratics over rational boxes is NP-hard. Hence the syntactic property \(f=g-h\) does not identify a tractable global-optimization class. Tractability requires additional restrictions on the decomposition, feasible geometry, dimension, or available bounding structure; unrestricted DC expressiveness crosses the NP-hardness boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DC form spans both tractable convex minimization and NP-hard concave quadratic minimization, so representation alone gives no tractability guarantee.
assumptions_latex: Problems use rational data or standard polynomial-time evaluation and separation oracles.
Exact global optimization is measured in the deterministic Turing model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f=g-h\) alone does not imply polynomial-time global minimizability unless \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\).

notation.meaning: convex components of a DC objective

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reverse-Convex Programming and Its Set-Difference Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a reverse-convex problem, preserves its boundary-inclusive constraint, and records the quasiconvex extension and dual relationship stated in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be finite convex functions and let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex. A reverse-convex program is \[\min\{f(x):x\in D,\ h(x)\ge 0\}.\] For \(C=\{x:h(x)\le 0\}\), its feasible set is \(D\setminus\operatorname{int}C\), so points with \(h(x)=0\) remain feasible. Equivalently, it minimizes \(t\) over \(G\setminus\operatorname{int}H\), where \(G=\{(x,t):x\in D,\ f(x)\le t\}\) and \(H=C\times\mathbb R\). The objective may be extended from convex to quasiconvex; in the stated nonconvex duality framework, quasiconvex minimization over complements of convex sets is dual to quasiconcave minimization over convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reverse-convex program minimizes a finite convex objective over a closed convex set while imposing a convex inequality in the reverse direction, h(x) at least zero. It can be written as optimization over a convex set with the interior of another convex set removed, retaining the boundary h(x)=0. The quasiconvex extension is dual to quasiconcave minimization over convex sets.
assumptions_latex: f,h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\text{ are finite convex functions}
D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is closed and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{f(x):x\in D,\ h(x)\ge 0\}=\min\{t:(x,t)\in G\setminus\operatorname{int}H\}

knowledge_statements.title: Concave Minimization over Polytopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme-point reduction for compact polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty compact polytope and let \(f:P\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous and concave. Then \(f\) attains its minimum on \(P\), and at least one minimizing point is a vertex of \(P\). Equivalently, \[\min_{x\in P}f(x)=\min_{v\in\operatorname{vert}(P)}f(v).\] The assertion guarantees an optimal vertex but does not assert that every minimizer is a vertex; for example, a constant concave function is minimized throughout \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous concave function on a compact polytope has an optimal vertex, so its minimum equals the minimum over all vertices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in P}f(x)=\min_{v\in\operatorname{vert}(P)}f(v)\).

notation.meaning: finite vertex set of the polytope P

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded-polyhedral regime for concave minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standing assumptions for the section's enumerative concave-minimization methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n\mid Cx=b,\ x\ge 0\} be a nonempty bounded polyhedron, where C\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n} and b\in\mathbb{R}^m. Let A\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be open and convex with D\subseteq A, and let f:A\to\mathbb{R} be concave. Assume that for every \alpha\in\mathbb{R}, the upper level set \{x\in A\mid f(x)\ge\alpha\} is bounded. Problem (P) is \min\{f(x)\mid x\in D\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The problem minimizes a concave function over a nonempty bounded polyhedron in equality-and-nonnegativity form, contained in an open convex domain; every upper level set of the objective is also assumed bounded.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-program representation of the convex envelope on a polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme-point formula for a real-valued concave function on a bounded polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\subseteq H\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty bounded polyhedron with extreme points \(v^1,\ldots,v^p\), and let \(h:H\to\mathbb R\) be concave. For every \(\bar x\in M\), \[h_M(\bar x)=\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_i h(v^i):\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_i v^i=\bar x,\ \sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_i=1,\ \lambda_i\ge0\right\},\] and the linear program has a finite optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a bounded polyhedron, the convex envelope of a real-valued concave function is obtained by minimizing convex combinations of its extreme-point values that represent the given point.
assumptions_latex: \varnothing\ne M\subseteq H\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is a bounded polyhedron}

knowledge_statements.title: Concave Minimization over Unbounded Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of finite attainment when a recession direction decreases the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty unbounded polyhedron. Concavity and continuity of \(f:P\to\mathbb{R}\) do not ensure a finite minimum. If there exist \(x_0\in P\), a nonzero recession direction \(d\) with \(x_0+td\in P\) for all \(t\geq0\), and constants \(a\in\mathbb{R}\), \(b>0\) such that \(f(x_0+td)\leq a-bt\), then \(\inf_{x\in P}f(x)=-\infty\). In particular, \(P=[0,\infty)\) and \(f(x)=-x\) satisfy this condition. Thus the compact-polytope extreme-point theorem cannot be transferred without recession analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an unbounded polyhedron, a decreasing recession ray can drive a continuous concave objective to negative infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(x_0+td\in P\) and \(f(x_0+td)\leq a-bt\) for all \(t\geq0\), with \(b>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in P}f(x)=-\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Drop Recession-Ray Criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp raywise condition forcing a concave objective to be unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron, let \(f:P\to\mathbb{R}\) be concave, and suppose \(d\neq0\) is a recession direction from \(x_0\in P\). If there exist \(0\le s<t\) such that \(f(x_0+td)<f(x_0+sd)\), then \[\inf_{u\ge0}f(x_0+ud)=-\infty,\qquad\text{and hence}\qquad\inf_{x\in P}f(x)=-\infty.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any strict decrease between two points on a feasible recession ray forces a concave objective to tend to negative infinity along that ray.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in P}f(x)=-\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unbounded Feasibility Does Not Imply an Unbounded Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converse failure showing that feasible-set unboundedness alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=[0,\infty)\) and \(f(x)=0\) for all \(x\in P\). Then \(P\) is an unbounded polyhedron and \(f\) is continuous and concave, but \[\min_{x\in P}f(x)=0,\qquad \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}f(x)=P.\] Thus an unbounded feasible polyhedron need not produce an unbounded-below or unattained concave-minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbounded polyhedron can have a finite attained concave minimum, so feasible-set unboundedness alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in P}f(x)=0\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}f(x)=P\).
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Feasibility Does Not Imply an Unbounded Objective

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Convex Feasible Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme-point attainment beyond polyhedral feasible regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous and concave. Then \(f\) attains its minimum on \(C\), and some minimizer is an extreme point of \(C\). Consequently, \[\min_{x\in C}f(x)=\min_{e\in\operatorname{ext}(C)}f(e).\] The extreme-point set need not be finite, so this equality is a structural reduction rather than a finite enumeration algorithm for general compact convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous concave function on a compact convex set attains its minimum at some extreme point, though there may be infinitely many extreme points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in C}f(x)=\min_{e\in\operatorname{ext}(C)}f(e)\).

notation.meaning: set of extreme points of C

knowledge_statements.title: Nonpolyhedral Convex Feasible Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme-point optimality persists, but finite vertex enumeration fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a compact nonpolyhedral convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), continuous concave minimization still admits an extreme-point minimizer, but \(\operatorname{ext}(C)\) may be infinite. For example, when \(n\geq2\), the Euclidean unit ball \(C=\{x:\lVert x\rVert_2\leq1\}\) is nonpolyhedral and every boundary point is extreme. For any \(c\neq0\), the linear, hence concave, objective \(f(x)=c^{\mathsf T}x\) has the unique minimizer \(x^*=-c/\lVert c\rVert_2\). Thus polytope-style finite vertex enumeration has no direct analogue on general nonpolyhedral convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extreme-point optimality survives on compact nonpolyhedral sets, but infinitely many extreme points prevent finite vertex enumeration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\arg\min_{\lVert x\rVert_2\leq1}c^{\mathsf T}x=\{-c/\lVert c\rVert_2\}\), while \(\operatorname{ext}(C)\) is infinite.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Concave Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional separable concave objectives over nonempty polyhedral feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,n\in\mathbb{N}\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(C=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}\) be nonempty. For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), define \(D_i=\{x_i:x\in C\}\) and let \(f_i:D_i\to\mathbb{R}\) be concave. A separable concave-minimization problem has the form
\[
\min\left\{f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i):x\in C\right\}.
\]
The resulting objective \(f\) is concave on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable concave-minimization problem minimizes a sum of univariate concave functions over a nonempty polyhedron; the resulting multivariate objective is concave on that polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: For every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(f_i:D_i\to\mathbb{R}\) is concave, where \(D_i=\{x_i:x\in C\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\) is concave on \(C\).

notation.meaning: projection of the feasible set onto coordinate i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Decomposition on Cartesian Feasible Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent-coordinate special case of separable concave minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(C=\prod_{i=1}^n C_i\neq\varnothing\) and every \(f_i\) attains its minimum on \(C_i\), then \[\min_{x\in C}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)=\sum_{i=1}^n\min_{t\in C_i}f_i(t),\qquad \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\sum_i f_i(x_i)=\prod_i\operatorname*{argmin}_{t\in C_i}f_i(t).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without coupling constraints, the separable problem decomposes exactly into independent univariate minimizations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_C\sum_i f_i=\sum_i\min_{C_i}f_i\), and the minimizer set is the product of the component minimizer sets.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinatewise Convex Envelope on a Box
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex envelope of a finite separable concave objective on a bounded Cartesian box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\prod_{i=1}^n[\ell_i,u_i]\), where \(\ell_i<u_i\), and let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\), with each \(f_i\) finite and concave on \([\ell_i,u_i]\). Define \(h_i(t)=\frac{u_i-t}{u_i-\ell_i}f_i(\ell_i)+\frac{t-\ell_i}{u_i-\ell_i}f_i(u_i)\). Then \[\operatorname{vex}_B f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n h_i(x_i).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a Cartesian box, the convex envelope of a separable concave objective is the sum of its coordinate endpoint chords.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is finite and concave on its coordinate interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{vex}_B(\sum_i f_i)(x)=\sum_i h_i(x_i)\).

notation.meaning: convex envelope of f on B

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise endpoint-interpolation formula over a rectangular domain, including possibly degenerate coordinate intervals.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chord-program lower bound on a rectangular subregion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint-chord lower bound for a separable concave objective over integer feasible points in a rectangular subregion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E^R=\{j\in E:c_j^R<d_j^R\}\) and \(C^R\subseteq E^R\). Suppose \(f(x)=\sum_{j\in E}f_j(x_j)\), where \(f_j\) is concave and nonlinear for \(j\in C^R\), and \(f_j(x_j)=\ell_jx_j\) for \(j\in E^R\setminus C^R\). For \(j\in E^R\), define \(u_j^R=d_j^R-c_j^R\), \(b^R=b-Ac^R\), let \(A^R\) consist of the columns \(A_j\) with \(j\in E^R\), and set \(\ell_j^R=(f_j(d_j^R)-f_j(c_j^R))/(d_j^R-c_j^R)\) for \(j\in C^R\), with \(\ell_j^R=\ell_j\) otherwise. If \(b^R\) and \(u^R\) are integral, then \[\mu^R=\sum_{j\in E}f_j(c_j^R)+\min\left\{\sum_{j\in E^R}\ell_j^Ry_j:A^Ry=b^R,\ 0\le y_j\le u_j^R\ (j\in E^R)\right\}\] is a lower bound for \(f\) over \(R\cap D\cap\mathbb Z^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On each varying nonlinear coordinate, replace the concave term by its endpoint chord; retain the varying linear terms unchanged. After shifting to the rectangle's lower corner, the resulting bounded linear program gives a lower bound on the objective over the feasible integer points in the rectangle.
assumptions_latex: f_j\text{ is concave and nonlinear for }j\in C^R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu^R\le f(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in R\cap D\cap\mathbb Z^n.

knowledge_statements.title: Concave Quadratic Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous finite-dimensional quadratic model with a negative-semidefinite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, and let \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n\), \(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(r\in\mathbb{R}\). A concave quadratic-minimization problem has the form
\[
\min\left\{f(x)=\tfrac12 x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+r:x\in C\right\},
\]
with \(Q\preceq0\). The Hessian of \(f\) is \(Q\), so \(f\) is concave on \(\mathbb{R}^n\); if \(Q\prec0\), then \(f\) is strictly concave.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Concave quadratic minimization minimizes a quadratic objective with a negative-semidefinite symmetric Hessian over a prescribed nonempty feasible set; a negative-definite Hessian makes the objective strictly concave.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic objective is concave on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and it is strictly concave when \(Q\prec0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unconstrained Concave-Quadratic Minimization Classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact unconstrained boundedness boundary for negative-semidefinite quadratics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+r\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), with \(Q\preceq0\). If \(Q=0\) and \(q=0\), then \(f\equiv r\) and every point is a global minimizer. In every other case, \[\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}f(x)=-\infty.\] In particular, when \(Q\prec0\), the stationary point \(-Q^{-1}q\) is the unique global maximizer, not a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unconstrained concave quadratic has a finite minimum only in the constant case; otherwise it is unbounded below, and a negative-definite stationary point is its maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((Q,q)=(0,0)\Rightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}f=\mathbb{R}^n\); otherwise \(\inf f=-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Concave-Quadratic Minimization Classification

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Completed-Square and Farthest-Point Formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical representation of negative-definite concave quadratic minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\prec0\), \(H=-Q\succ0\), and \(x_c=H^{-1}q\). Then \[\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+q^{\mathsf T}x+r=\left(r+\tfrac12q^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}q\right)-\tfrac12(x-x_c)^{\mathsf T}H(x-x_c).\] Consequently, for every nonempty \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in C}(x-x_c)^{\mathsf T}H(x-x_c).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-definite concave quadratic is a constant minus a positive-definite squared distance, making its minimization an equivalent farthest-point problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in C}(x-x_c)^{\mathsf T}H(x-x_c)\).

notation.meaning: positive-definite matrix equal to minus the quadratic Hessian

Quasiconcave-Minimization Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extreme-point minimization for real-valued quasiconcave objectives on finite-dimensional polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty polytope with vertex set \(\operatorname{ext}(C)=\{v^1,\ldots,v^m\}\), and let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be quasiconcave, meaning that
\[
f(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y)\ge\min\{f(x),f(y)\}
\]
for all \(x,y\in C\) and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\). Then
\[
\min_{x\in C}f(x)=\min_{1\le i\le m}f(v^i).
\]
In particular, this property applies to every concave real-valued function on \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real-valued quasiconcave function on a nonempty polytope has a global minimizer at a vertex. The result includes concave objectives as a special case.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in C}f(x)=\min_{1\le i\le m}f(v^i)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Definitions of Quasiconcavity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent finite-dimensional formulations used by the quasiconcave-minimization interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex and \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\). Then \(f\) is quasiconcave if and only if every upper level set \[U_\alpha=\{x\in C:f(x)\geq\alpha\}\] is convex. Equivalently, \[f(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y)\geq\min\{f(x),f(y)\}\] for all \(x,y\in C\) and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\). Every concave function is quasiconcave, but the converse need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quasiconcavity is equivalent to convexity of every upper level set and is weaker than concavity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\text{ is quasiconcave}\iff \{x\in C:f(x)\geq\alpha\}\text{ is convex for every }\alpha\in\mathbb{R}.\)

notation.meaning: upper level set at level alpha

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The notation presupposes that the real-valued convex envelope is well-defined; without an appropriate lower-boundedness or extended-real convention, the displayed infimum can equal \(-\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-Everywhere Differentiability of Concave Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General regularity of finite concave functions on open convex domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:H\to\mathbb{R}\) be concave, where \(H=\mathbb{R}^n\) or \(H\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and convex. For every \(x\in H\), either \(h\) is differentiable at \(x\), or there exists a sequence \((x_k)\subset H\) converging to \(x\) such that \(h\) is differentiable at every \(x_k\), or both. Moreover, the set of points where \(h\) is not differentiable has Lebesgue measure zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every point is a differentiability point or a limit of differentiability points, possibly both, and the nondifferentiability set has measure zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^m\}\) be a nonempty polytope and let \(f:P\to\mathbb{R}\) be concave. Then
\[
\min_{x\in P}f(x)=\min_{1\le i\le m}f(v^i).
\]
In particular, the minimum is attained, and at least one minimizer belongs to \(\operatorname{ext}(P)\). The assertion does not require strict concavity or uniqueness of the minimizing extreme point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every concave real-valued function on a nonempty polytope has a global minimizer at an extreme point of that polytope.

knowledge_statements.title: Face-Restriction Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constancy at the global minimum on a face whose relative interior contains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, let \(F\) be a nonempty face of \(C\), and let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be concave. If a global minimizer \(x^\star\) of \(f\) over \(C\) belongs to \(\operatorname{relint}(F)\), then
\[
f(y)=f(x^\star)=\min_{x\in C}f(x)
\]
for every \(y\in F\). Thus the restriction of \(f\) to \(F\) is constant at the global minimum value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a global minimizer of a concave objective lies in the relative interior of a face, the objective is constant at its global minimum value throughout that face.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex and \(F\) is a nonempty face of \(C\).
\(x^\star\in\operatorname{relint}(F)\) is a global minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every point of \(F\) is a global minimizer of \(f\) over \(C\).

notation.meaning: face containing a minimizer in its relative interior

knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Interior Hypothesis Is Essential
Recession-Direction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unboundedness caused by strict descent along an infinite feasible ray for a concave objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex, let \(x\in C\), and let \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\) satisfy \(x+td\in C\) for every \(t\ge0\). If \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is concave and
\[
f(x+t_0d)<f(x)
\]
for some \(t_0>0\), then
\[
\inf_{y\in C}f(y)=-\infty.
\]
Consequently, finite lower boundedness excludes strict descent along any such feasible recession ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a concave objective, a strict decrease along an infinite feasible ray makes the problem unbounded below. Hence a finite lower bound rules out such ray descent.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex, \(x\in C\), and \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\) satisfies \(x+td\in C\) for every \(t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{y\in C}f(y)=-\infty\).

notation.meaning: direction of an infinite feasible ray from the base point
positive ray parameter at which strict descent occurs

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and compact and \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous, then \(\min_{x\in C}f(x)\) is attained. Closedness and convexity without boundedness are insufficient: let
\[
C=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^2:xy\ge1\},\qquad f(x,y)=x.
\]
The set \(C\) is closed and convex as a subset of \(\mathbb{R}^2\), and \(f\) is linear, hence concave. Nevertheless,
\[
\inf_{(x,y)\in C}f(x,y)=0,
\]
and no feasible point attains this value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuity on a compact feasible set ensures attainment, but a continuous linear objective can have a finite unattained infimum on a closed unbounded convex set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact Sublevel Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient attainment condition weaker than compactness of the whole feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and closed and let \(f:C\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty compact sublevel set suffices for attainment even when the feasible set is unbounded.
assumptions_latex: For some \(\alpha\), \(S_\alpha\) is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\neq\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modified omega-partitioning rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A periodic geometry-based modification of omega-partitioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(N\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\). If \(L(s_k)\bmod N=0\), choose \[j'\in\arg\max_{j\in\mathcal J}(u_j^{s_k}-l_j^{s_k}),\qquad p=\frac{u_{j'}^{s_k}-l_{j'}^{s_k}}{2}.\] Otherwise choose \(j'\) and \(p\) by the unmodified \(\omega\)-partitioning rule. In either case, split \(C^{s_k}\) at coordinate \(j'\) and point \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a positive integer N, every Nth designated level selects a longest edge and uses half its length as the stated split value; at all other levels it uses ordinary omega-partitioning, then splits the current subdomain accordingly.
assumptions_latex: \(L(s_k)\) is the level associated with the current subdomain \(C^{s_k}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C^{s_k}\) is split at \((p,j')\), using the longest-edge rule when \(L(s_k)\equiv0\pmod N\) and the unmodified rule otherwise.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinate contraction from separable objective bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses objective bounds and monotone inverse branches of a concave coordinate function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For coordinate \(h\), compute \[\Delta_h^U=U-\sum_{j\ne h}\min\{f_j(u_j^s),f_j(l_j^s)\},\qquad \Delta_h^L=L-\sum_{j\ne h}\max_{x_j\in[l_j^s,u_j^s]}f_j(x_j).\] If \(f_h(x_h^{(A)})=\Delta_h^U\) on a decreasing branch and no corresponding increasing-branch point exists, impose \(x_h\ge x_h^{(A)}\). If \(f_h(x_h^{(B)})=\Delta_h^U\) on an increasing branch and no corresponding decreasing-branch point exists, impose \(x_h\le x_h^{(B)}\). If both points exist, impose \(x_h\le x_h^{(B)}\vee x_h\ge x_h^{(A)}\). If \(f_h(x_h^{(C)})=\Delta_h^L\) on a decreasing branch, impose \(x_h\le x_h^{(C)}\); if \(f_h(x_h^{(D)})=\Delta_h^L\) on an increasing branch, impose \(x_h\ge x_h^{(D)}\). In the one-to-two inverse case with lower and upper forks \(f_h^{-1L}\) and \(f_h^{-1U}\), reduce the coordinate domain to \[[l_h^s,u_h^s]\cap\left([f_h^{-1L}(\Delta_h^L),f_h^{-1L}(\Delta_h^U)]\cup[f_h^{-1U}(\Delta_h^U),f_h^{-1U}(\Delta_h^L)]\right),\] which may be disconnected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective bounds for a separable concave function induce coordinate restrictions through the decreasing and increasing branches of a component function. When its inverse has two branches, the surviving domain may be a union of two intervals.
assumptions_latex: f(x)=\sum_j f_j(x_j)\text{ with concave univariate components on }[l_j^s,u_j^s]
U\text{ and }L\text{ are the applicable upper and lower objective bounds}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_h\text{ satisfies each applicable branch restriction; in the stated one-to-two inverse case it lies in the displayed possibly disconnected contraction}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LP-based coordinate-bound preprocessing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replaces infinite coordinate bounds, and optionally tightens finite bounds, using exact coordinate extrema over the feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each $j$ with $l_j=-\infty$, solve $\min\{x_j:x\in D\cap C\}$ and replace $l_j$ by its optimal value. For each $j$ with $u_j=+\infty$, solve $\max\{x_j:x\in D\cap C\}$ and replace $u_j$ by its optimal value. Record feasible solutions encountered while solving these linear programs for preliminary bounding of the concave objective. The same procedure may optionally be applied to coordinates with finite bounds to tighten the formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace each missing lower or upper coordinate bound by the corresponding minimum or maximum over the feasible region. Feasible points encountered by these linear programs are retained for preliminary objective bounds. The same coordinate optimizations may optionally tighten bounds that are already finite.
assumptions_latex: \text{Each coordinate LP used to replace an infinite endpoint has a finite attained optimum.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{After all infinite endpoints are replaced, the feasible set has an equivalent bounded-box representation; optional exact coordinate tightening preserves the feasible set.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Branch-and-Reduce Procedure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded algorithmic sketch for global minimization of a separable concave program; the extract does not state a termination rule or convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Preprocess the problem by solving linear programs to bound unbounded variables and, optionally, tighten existing bounds. Use feasible points found during preprocessing to initialize an upper bound \(U\), and apply Techniques 5 and 6 to the original domain \(C\). At iteration \(k\), select an open subproblem \(s_k\), apply Techniques 1--6, and compute \(\alpha^{s_k}\) and a revised \(\beta^{s_k}\) such that \[\alpha^{s_k}\geq \min\{f(x):x\in D\cap C^{s_k}\}\geq \beta^{s_k}.\] Then set \[U\leftarrow\min_{s\in\mathcal S}\alpha^s,\qquad L\leftarrow\min_{s\in\mathcal S}\beta^s.\] If \(U\) improves, apply Techniques 1--6 to all open subproblems in \(\mathcal S\); otherwise apply them only to \(s_k\). If domain reduction succeeds, repeat the bounding-and-reduction step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use linear programs during preprocessing to bound unbounded variables and optionally tighten existing bounds. Initialize an upper bound from feasible preprocessing points and reduce the original domain. At each iteration, select an open subproblem, compute an upper and lower bound for its minimum, and update the global values by taking the minimum respective bounds over the open subproblems. Apply the reduction techniques to every open subproblem after an upper-bound improvement and only to the selected subproblem otherwise. Repeat the step when domain reduction succeeds.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal S\text{ is the current set of open regional subproblems.}
\alpha^s\geq \min\{f(x):x\in D\cap C^s\}\geq \beta^s\text{ for each open subproblem whose bounds enter the updates.}
\text{Techniques 1--6 are the bounding and domain-reduction operations defined elsewhere in the source.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U\leftarrow\min_{s\in\mathcal S}\alpha^s,\qquad L\leftarrow\min_{s\in\mathcal S}\beta^s,\quad\text{with global reduction after an improvement of }U\text{ and local reduction otherwise.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cuts from inactive variable bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partially restricted relaxations derive cuts from inactive upper and lower domain bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x_j\le u_j^s\) is inactive at \(\omega^s\), let \[g^s(\omega^r)=\min\{g^s(x):x\in D\cap C^s,\ x_j=u_j^s\}.\] If the imposed boundary has multiplier \(\lambda_j>0\), then \[x_j\le u_j^s-\frac{U-g^s(\omega^r)}{\lambda_j}\] is valid for \(s\). Similarly, if \(x_j\ge l_j^s\) is inactive and the restriction \(x_j=l_j^s\) has multiplier \(\lambda_j>0\), then, as extracted, \[x_j\ge l_j^s-\frac{U-g^s(\omega^r)}{\lambda_j}\] is valid for \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing an inactive domain bound and solving the resulting partially restricted relaxation yields a subproblem-valid bound when the imposed boundary has a positive multiplier. The extracted lower-bound case uses a minus sign and is preserved without correction.
assumptions_latex: x_j\le u_j^s\text{ or }x_j\ge l_j^s\text{ is inactive at }\omega^s
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_j\le u_j^s-\frac{U-g^s(\omega^r)}{\lambda_j}\quad\text{or, respectively,}\quad x_j\ge l_j^s-\frac{U-g^s(\omega^r)}{\lambda_j}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Periodic longest-edge and underestimation-gap branching rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Literal extraction-grounded branching operation; the fallback formula is a half-width, not necessarily the interval midpoint, and yields a valid split only when it lies in the selected interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $C^{s_k}=\prod_{j=1}^n[l_j^{s_k},u_j^{s_k}]$. If $L(s_k)\bmod N=0$, choose $j'\in\arg\max_{j\in\mathcal J}(u_j^{s_k}-l_j^{s_k})$; otherwise choose $j'\in\arg\max_{j\in\mathcal J}\bigl[f_j(\omega_j^{s_k})-g_j^{s_k}(\omega_j^{s_k})\bigr]$. If $\widetilde x\in C^{s_k}$ and $\widetilde x_{j'}\in(l_{j'}^{s_k},u_{j'}^{s_k})$, set $p=\widetilde x_{j'}$; otherwise set $p=(u_{j'}^{s_k}-l_{j'}^{s_k})/2$. When $p\in[l_{j'}^{s_k},u_{j'}^{s_k}]$, split the rectangle into $[l_{j'}^{s_k},p]\prod_{j\ne j'}[l_j^{s_k},u_j^{s_k}]$ and $[p,u_{j'}^{s_k}]\prod_{j\ne j'}[l_j^{s_k},u_j^{s_k}]$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the stated level counter is divisible by N, branch on a longest edge; otherwise branch on a coordinate with the largest underestimation gap. Split at an interior reference-point coordinate when available. Otherwise the extract uses the half-width (upper minus lower divided by two), which is not generally the midpoint and may fail to lie in the interval. The two-child rectangular partition is valid only when the selected split value lies in that interval.
assumptions_latex: L(s_k),\ f_j(\omega_j^{s_k}),\text{ and }g_j^{s_k}(\omega_j^{s_k})\text{ are defined for the stated selections.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\in[l_{j'}^{s_k},u_{j'}^{s_k}]\implies C^{s_k}=\left([l_{j'}^{s_k},p]\prod_{j\ne j'}[l_j^{s_k},u_j^{s_k}]\right)\cup\left([p,u_{j'}^{s_k}]\prod_{j\ne j'}[l_j^{s_k},u_j^{s_k}]\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modified Kalantari–Rosen Partitioning Operation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-specific branching operation for an enumeration-cutting algorithm for separable concave minimization. The fallback split formula is retained exactly as extracted; it is half the interval width, not the usual interval midpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose
\[
j'\in\arg\max_{j\in\mathcal J}\lambda_j\bigl(u_j^{s_k}-l_j^{s_k}\bigr)^2.
\]
If \(\widetilde x\in C^{s_k}\) and \(\widetilde x_{j'}\in(l_{j'}^{s_k},u_{j'}^{s_k})\), set \(p=\widetilde x_{j'}\). Otherwise set
\[
p=\frac{u_{j'}^{s_k}-l_{j'}^{s_k}}{2}.
\]
Split \(C^{s_k}\) at \(p\) along coordinate \(j'\). As printed, the fallback formula does not by itself guarantee \(p\in[l_{j'}^{s_k},u_{j'}^{s_k}]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a coordinate maximizing its weight times the squared interval width. Use the corresponding coordinate of the candidate point when the point belongs to the current region and that coordinate is strictly interior; otherwise use half the interval width, exactly as printed. Then split along the selected coordinate. Without an additional condition on the bounds, the printed fallback need not lie inside the interval.
assumptions_latex: \lambda_j,\ l_j^{s_k},\ u_j^{s_k}\text{ are defined for every }j\in\mathcal J

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bound-and-branch algorithm for separable concave minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maintains open rectangular subproblems and uses valid upper and lower bounds for termination and fathoming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Preprocess $D\cap C$ to obtain a bounded hyperrectangle $C^0$, initialize $\mathcal S$ with $\min\{f(x):x\in D\cap C^0\}$, and choose $N\in\mathbb N$, $N<\infty$. At iteration $k$, remove a selected subproblem $s_k$ from $\mathcal S$ and compute bounds $\alpha^{s_k}\ge \min\{f(x):x\in D\cap C^{s_k}\}\ge\beta^{s_k}$, with $\alpha^{s_k}=\beta^{s_k}=+\infty$ when $D\cap C^{s_k}=\varnothing$; if $\beta^{s_k}<+\infty$, obtain $x^{s_k}\in D\cap C^{s_k}$ satisfying $f(x^{s_k})=\alpha^{s_k}$. Set $U=\min_{s\in\mathcal S}\alpha^s$ and $L=\min_{s\in\mathcal S}\beta^s$. If $U=L$, terminate with an optimal solution. Delete every $s$ with $\beta^s\ge U$; if $\beta^{s_k}\ge U$, select another subproblem. Otherwise partition $C^{s_k}$ into $C^{s_{k1}}$ and $C^{s_{k2}}$ such that $C^{s_{k1}}\cup C^{s_{k2}}=C^{s_k}$ and $C^{s_{k1}}\cap C^{s_{k2}}=\partial C^{s_{k1}}\cap\partial C^{s_{k2}}$, append both children, and initialize $\beta^{s_{k1}}=\beta^{s_{k2}}=\beta^{s_k}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start with a bounded rectangular domain and a list containing the original subproblem. Repeatedly select and remove an open subproblem, compute a feasible-point upper bound and a valid lower bound, terminate when the global upper and lower bounds coincide, discard nodes whose lower bounds cannot improve the incumbent upper bound, and otherwise bisect the selected rectangle and add its two children with the inherited lower bound. An infeasible subproblem is assigned infinite upper and lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: C^0\text{ is a bounded hyperrectangle containing the relevant portion of }D\cap C.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U=L\implies\text{termination with a globally optimal solution; nodes satisfying }\beta^s\ge U\text{ may be fathomed.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a nonempty polytope \(P\) and a concave evaluable function \(f:P\to\mathbb{R}\). Enumerate \(V=\operatorname{ext}(P)=\{v^1,\ldots,v^m\}\), evaluate \(f(v^i)\), and order the vertices so that
\[
f(v^{(1)})\le f(v^{(2)})\le\cdots\le f(v^{(m)}).
\]
Initialize \(v^{\mathrm{best}}=v^{(1)}\) and \(U=f(v^{(1)})\). Stop after all vertices have been evaluated and output \((v^{\mathrm{best}},U)\). Extreme-point attainment yields
\[
U=f(v^{\mathrm{best}})=\min_{x\in P}f(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate all vertices of the feasible polytope, evaluate and rank them by objective value, and return the lowest-ranked vertex as a global minimizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a simplex \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v^0,\ldots,v^n\}\), write \(x=\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i(x)v^i\) and define
\[
\ell_S(x)=\sum_{i=0}^n\lambda_i(x)f(v^i).
\]
Concavity gives \(\ell_S(x)\le f(x)\) on \(S\). Compute \(L_S=\min_{x\in S}\ell_S(x)\). If \(L_S\ge U\), cut off \(S\); otherwise evaluate selected feasible points, update \(U\), and subdivide \(S\). Stop when no active simplex remains or every active bound satisfies \(U-L_S\le\varepsilon\); output the incumbent and its certified gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use affine chords beneath a concave objective to bound each simplex, prune simplices that cannot improve the incumbent, and subdivide the rest.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Iterative coordinatewise cut-improvement procedure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded cut-improvement algorithm using coordinate auxiliary minimizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from the referenced \(\gamma\)-valid cut with intercept vector \(t\): (1) compute \(y^i\in\operatorname{argmin}\{F(t_i e^i,y)\mid y\in M(t)\}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\); (2) if \(f(y^i)<\gamma\) for some \(i\), set \(\gamma':=\min_{1\leq i\leq n}f(y^i)\) and construct a \(\gamma'\)-valid cut with the new incumbent; (3) otherwise compute \(t_i^*\) by (10.43) and construct the cut \(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i/t_i^*\geq1\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Majthay–Whinston combination-cut algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An enumerative concave-minimization method combining local extreme-point search, objective-valid cuts, facial cuts, and relative extreme-face detection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize M=\mathbb{R}^n at an extreme point v^\circ\in D, set \gamma=f(v^\circ), and retain v^\circ as incumbent. Repeatedly perform a simplex-based search for an extreme point locally minimizing f over D\cap M and update the incumbent when its value is below \gamma. Eliminate the current point by a \gamma-valid Tuy cut when it is nondegenerate, or by a weaker \gamma-valid cut otherwise. Find a basic feasible solution of D\cap M by dual simplex or parametric programming and apply the extreme-face search routine. If the routine returns a proper positive-dimensional extreme face F, add a facial cut eliminating F; if it returns an extreme point, resume the point search from that extreme point. If D\cap M=\varnothing or the returned face is D, terminate with the incumbent as a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The algorithm alternates local search over extreme points with objective-valid point cuts and facial cuts. It maintains the best incumbent, restores feasibility after adding cuts, and uses relative extreme-face detection to decide whether to search from another extreme point or eliminate an entire face. Exhaustion of the remaining region, or detection of the whole feasible polyhedron as the relative extreme face, certifies the incumbent as globally optimal.

v^\circ\in D\text{ is an extreme point}
\text{The stated local-search, valid-cut, feasibility-recovery, and extreme-face routines are available}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\cap M=\varnothing\ \text{or}\ F=D\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{\mathrm{inc}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D}f(x).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(P_0\supseteq C\), a feasible incumbent \(\bar x\in C\), and \(U_0=f(\bar x)\). At iteration \(k\), choose
\[
v_k\in\arg\min\{f(v):v\in\operatorname{ext}(P_k)\},\qquad L_k=f(v_k).

If \(v_k\in C\), update the incumbent and stop globally. Otherwise obtain \(a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta_k\), valid for every \(x\in C\) but violated by \(v_k\), and set
\[
P_{k+1}=P_k\cap\{x:a_k^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta_k\}.
\]
Stop when \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\), returning the incumbent and gap certificate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: General cutting-function outer-approximation scheme
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative outer approximation for \((P):\min\{f(x):x\in D\}\), with an ambient set \(A\supseteq D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a compact set \(D_1\subseteq A\) with \(D\subseteq D_1\). For \(k=1,2,\ldots\), compute \(x^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in D_k}f(x)\). Otherwise choose \(q_k:A\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(q_k(x)\leq0\) for every \(x\in D\) and \(q_k(x^k)>0\), and set \(D_{k+1}=D_k\cap\{x\in A:q_k(x)\leq0\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Annexation for Concave Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic polyhedral-annexation scheme for minimizing a concave function over a compact polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a compact polytope \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^n\), a concave function \(f:P\to\mathbb{R}\), an initial polytope \(Q_0\subseteq P\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), set \(U_0=+\infty\). At iteration \(k\), minimize \(f\) over the vertices of \(Q_k\), update \(U_k\) with the best feasible value found, and obtain a valid lower bound \(L_k\leq\min_{x\in P}f(x)\) for the unexplored region. If \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\), return the incumbent. Otherwise annex a polyhedral region containing a selected unexplored candidate, producing \(Q_{k+1}\supsetneq Q_k\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successively enlarge an explored polytope, evaluate its vertices, maintain a valid unexplored-region bound, and stop when the incumbent–bound gap is within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Each annexation and lower-bound computation is valid for the remaining region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination with \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\) certifies an \(\varepsilon\)-global minimizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonexhaustive Annexation Can Preserve a Positive Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of convergence when nested annexed polytopes omit a neighborhood of the optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=[0,1]\), \(f(x)=x\), and \(Q_k=[\tfrac12+\tfrac1{k+3},1]\). Then \(Q_k\subsetneq Q_{k+1}\subset P\), and exact vertex minimization over \(Q_k\) gives \(U_k=\tfrac12+\tfrac1{k+3}\to\tfrac12\). Since the residual set contains \(0\), the value \(b_k=0\) is a valid residual lower bound. Thus the certified global lower bound \(\underline L_k=\min\{U_k,b_k\}=0\) and \(U_k-\underline L_k\to\tfrac12\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence Under Exhaustive Polyhedral Annexation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient exhaustion and residual-bound consistency conditions for the accepted annexation scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a compact polytope, \(f:P\to\mathbb R\) continuous and concave, and \(Q_k\subseteq Q_{k+1}\subseteq P\) nonempty compact polytopes. Let \(U_k=\min_{x\in Q_k}f(x)\), obtained by evaluating the vertices of \(Q_k\). Let \(b_k\le\inf_{x\in P\setminus Q_k}f(x)\) when the residual is nonempty, set \(b_k=+\infty\) otherwise, and define \(\underline L_k=\min\{U_k,b_k\}\). If the Hausdorff distance from \(Q_k\) to \(P\) tends to zero and \(\liminf_k b_k\ge f^*=\min_P f\), then \(U_k\to f^*\), \(\underline L_k\to f^*\), and \(U_k-\underline L_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hausdorff exhaustion and consistent residual bounds make the annexation certificate gap converge to zero.
assumptions_latex: The nested annexed polytopes converge to \(P\) in Hausdorff distance.
Residual lower bounds are valid and have limit inferior at least \(f^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral annexation as inner approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner-approximation counterpart of outer approximation for concave minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Outer approximation uses nested supersets \(O_1\supset O_2\supset\cdots\supset D\), and the minima of \(f\) over \(O_k\) are nondecreasing and approach the optimal value \(v\) from below. Polyhedral annexation uses nested polyhedral inner approximations \(I_1\subset I_2\subset\cdots\subset D\), and the minima of \(f\) over \(I_k\) are nonincreasing and approach \(v\) from above. In the formalized polyhedral setting, assume that \(D\) is a nonempty bounded polyhedron, \(A\supseteq D\) is open and convex, and \(\{x\in A:f(x)\geq\alpha\}\) is bounded for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\). The inner approximations have the form \(I_k=P_k\cap D\), where \(P_1\subset P_2\subset\cdots\) are expanding bounded polyhedra that may contain points both in and outside \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outer approximation shrinks supersets and yields lower values increasing to the optimum. Polyhedral annexation expands polyhedral subsets and yields upper values decreasing to the optimum. In its formalized setting, the feasible region is a nonempty bounded polyhedron and each inner approximation is its intersection with an expanding bounded polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: D\text{ is a nonempty bounded polyhedron}
A\supseteq D\text{ is open and convex}
\{x\in A:f(x)\geq\alpha\}\text{ is bounded for every }\alpha\in\mathbb R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I_k=P_k\cap D,\quad I_1\subset I_2\subset\cdots\subset D,\quad \min_{x\in I_k}f(x)\downarrow v;\qquad O_1\supset O_2\supset\cdots\supset D,\quad \min_{x\in O_k}f(x)\uparrow v.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polyhedral Annexation algorithm for BCP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral-annexation scheme for the source's BCP model, using convex objective superlevel sets and DC* as a set-containment oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \((BCP)\), compute a vertex \(\bar x\) of \(D\), define \(C=\{x:f(x)\ge f(\bar x)\}\), and call \(DC^*\) with an initial vertex \(x^0\) satisfying \(f(x^0)>f(\bar x)\). If \(DC^*\) returns \(z\in D\setminus C\), set \(\bar x\leftarrow z\) and repeat; optionally, with \(\gamma=f(z)\), construct a \(\gamma\)-valid cut \(\pi(x-x^0)\ge1\) and replace \(D\) by \(D\cap\{x:\pi(x-x^0)\ge1\}\). If \(DC^*\) establishes \(D\subset C\), return \(\bar x\) as an optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The PA algorithm repeatedly uses DC* to search for a feasible point with a lower objective value than the current vertex incumbent. A returned improving point becomes the new incumbent, optionally with a valid cut; a containment certificate proves the incumbent globally optimal.

knowledge_statements.title: Successive Underestimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bounding scheme using increasingly accurate underestimators of a concave objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and compact, let \(f:P\to\mathbb{R}\) be concave, define \(f^*=\min_{x\in P}f(x)\), and fix \(\varepsilon\geq0\). Choose functions \(g_k:P\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(g_k(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in P\), and compute \(x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}g_k(x)\) with \(L_k=g_k(x_k)\). Evaluate \(f(x_k)\) and set \(U_k=\min_{0\leq j\leq k}f(x_j)\). If \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\), return an incumbent attaining \(U_k\); otherwise choose \(g_{k+1}\geq g_k\) that remains a global underestimator and is exact at the selected evaluated points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize nested global lower models, evaluate their minimizers in the true objective, and refine until the incumbent–lower-bound gap meets the requested tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Each lower-model problem attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every iteration, \(L_k\leq f^*\leq U_k\); hence \(U_k-L_k\leq\varepsilon\) certifies that the returned incumbent is \(\varepsilon\)-globally optimal.

notation.meaning: global minimum of f over P

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Exactness Alone Does Not Ensure Value Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for schemes exact only at finitely many sampled points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(P=[0,1]\), let \(f\equiv0\), choose distinct sample points \(s_0,s_1,\ldots\), and define \(g_k(x)=0\) for \(x\in\{s_0,\ldots,s_k\}\) and \(g_k(x)=-1\) otherwise. Then \(g_k\leq g_{k+1}\leq f\) and \(g_k\) is exact at every sampled point, but \(\min_P g_k=-1\) for every finite \(k\), whereas \(\min_P f=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested underestimators can be exact at every sampled point while their lower bounds fail to converge to the true optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(g_k\) is defined by the displayed sampled-point rule.

notation.meaning: sample point at which the model is exact

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniformly Consistent Underestimator Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of lower-model values under uniform approximation from below.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be nonempty and compact and let \(g_k:P\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfy \(g_k\leq g_{k+1}\leq f\). Define \(L_k=\min_{x\in P}g_k(x)\) and \(f^*=\min_{x\in P}f(x)\), assuming these minima exist. If \(\|f-g_k\|_{\infty,P}\to0\), then \(L_k\uparrow f^*\). If feasible incumbent values satisfy \(U_k\downarrow f^*\), then \(U_k-L_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested global underestimators converging uniformly to the objective yield monotonically convergent lower bounds and a vanishing gap with consistent incumbents.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\uparrow f^*\), and \(U_k-L_k\to0\) if \(U_k\downarrow f^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Construction of a Concavity-Cut Hyperplane
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructs the hyperplane through the intersections of a containing simplicial cone's edges with a bounded concave upper-level set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a full-dimensional feasible polyhedron, let \(C(\gamma)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:f(x)\ge\gamma\}\) be bounded, and let \(x^0\) be a vertex of \(D\) with \(f(x^0)>\gamma\). Suppose that a cone \(M\), vertexed at \(x^0\), contains \(D\) and has exactly \(n\) linearly independent edges. If those edges meet \(\partial C(\gamma)\) at \(z^1,\ldots,z^n\), then the points are affinely independent. For \(Q=[z^1-x^0,\ldots,z^n-x^0]\) and \(e=(1,\ldots,1)\), \(Q\) is nonsingular and the hyperplane through the \(z^i\) is \[\pi(x-x^0)=1,\qquad \pi=eQ^{-1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A containing simplicial cone at a feasible vertex determines boundary points on a bounded concave upper-level set. These points are affinely independent, and their hyperplane has coefficient row eQ inverse.
assumptions_latex: D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is a full-dimensional feasible polyhedron}
D\subseteq M,\quad M\text{ is a cone vertexed at }x^0\text{ with exactly }n\text{ linearly independent edges}
z^i\text{ is the intersection of edge }i\text{ with }\partial C(\gamma)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z^1,\ldots,z^n\text{ are affinely independent},\quad Q=[z^1-x^0,\ldots,z^n-x^0]\text{ is nonsingular},\quad \pi=eQ^{-1}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Prototype successive partitioning algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic global minimization over D using a partition of a closed region containing D.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a closed set M_0 with D\subseteq M_0\subseteq A, initialize \mathcal P_0=\{M_0\}, choose \beta_0=\beta(M_0)\leq\min_{x\in M_0}f(x), and set \alpha_0=f(x^\circ) if a point x^\circ\in M_0\cap D is available and \alpha_0=+\infty otherwise. At iteration k, fathom each active M satisfying \beta(M)\geq\alpha_{k-1} or for which f(x)\geq v for all x\in M. If no active element remains, terminate. Otherwise select M_k, partition it into R(M_k), and for each child M choose bounds satisfying \beta(M_k)\leq\beta(M)\leq\min_{x\in M\cap D}f(x)\leq\alpha(M), with \alpha(M)=\min_{x\in S_M}f(x) for a finite set S_M\subseteq M\cap D containing inherited samples and with \min\varnothing=+\infty. Set \mathcal P_k=(\mathcal P_{k-1}\setminus\{M_k\})\cup R(M_k), \alpha_k=\min_{M\in\mathcal P_k}\alpha(M), and \beta_k=\min_{M\in\mathcal P_k}\beta(M). If \alpha_k<+\infty, choose an incumbent x^k attaining \alpha_k. Terminate when \alpha_k=\beta_k; then x^k is globally optimal and v=\alpha_k=\beta_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain valid lower and feasible-point upper bounds on an active partition. Fathom regions unable to improve the incumbent, subdivide one remaining region, update its children and the global bounds, and terminate with a global optimum when the active partition becomes empty or the bounds coincide.
assumptions_latex: D\subseteq M_0\subseteq A\text{ and }M_0\text{ is closed}
\beta(M)\leq\min_{x\in M\cap D}f(x)\leq\alpha(M)\text{ for every active partition element }M
S_M\subseteq M\cap D\text{ is finite and contains inherited feasible samples}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_k=\beta_k\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x^k\text{ is globally optimal and }v=\alpha_k=\beta_k

knowledge_statements.title: Simplicial Successive Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplicial branch-and-bound using affine vertex interpolants as concave-objective lower models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition a compact polytope \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) into simplices. For a simplex \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0,\ldots,v_n\}\), define its affine interpolant by \(\ell_S(\sum_i\lambda_i v_i)=\sum_i\lambda_i f(v_i)\), where \(\lambda_i\geq0\) and \(\sum_i\lambda_i=1\). Concavity gives \(\ell_S(x)\leq f(x)\) on \(S\), so \(L(S)=\min_i f(v_i)\) is a node lower bound. Select a live simplex, subdivide it simplicially, evaluate new vertices, update the incumbent, and fathom any child whose bound is no smaller than the incumbent minus \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursively split the domain into simplices and use affine interpolation of vertex values to bound and discard subregions.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a compact polytope admitting a finite simplicial partition.
Subdivision preserves a conforming cover of every live region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each node satisfies \(L(S)\leq\min_{x\in S}f(x)\), making the stated fathoming test valid.

affine interpolant through the simplex vertices
valid lower bound for simplex S

knowledge_statements.title: Rectangular Successive Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangle-based spatial branching with valid regional lower bounds for concave minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_0=[l,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty compact box, let \(f:R_0\to\mathbb{R}\) be finite and concave, define \(f^*=\min_{x\in R_0}f(x)\), and fix \(\varepsilon\geq0\). Maintain a collection of live boxes. For every live box \(R\), compute a valid bound \(L(R)\leq\min_{x\in R}f(x)\) and a feasible point \(z_R\in R\), and update the incumbent value \(U\) using \(f(z_R)\). Select a live box with smallest bound, choose \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(s\in(l_j,u_j)\), and replace the box by the two children defined by \(x_j\leq s\) and \(x_j\geq s\). Discard every box satisfying \(L(R)\geq U-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split live boxes, compute valid regional lower bounds and feasible values, and discard boxes that cannot improve the incumbent by more than the tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The regional bounding rule is valid on every generated box, and the children cover their parent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every point \(x\) satisfying \(f(x)<U-\varepsilon\) remains in a live box; therefore an empty live set implies \(U-f^*\leq\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: C-integral rectangular bisection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer-lattice-preserving bisection along a widest coordinate from the designated coordinate set \(C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A subdivision of \(M=[r,s]\) via \((v,j)\) is called a bisection of ratio \(\alpha\) when \(j\) corresponds to a longest side of \(M\), \(v\) is a point of that side, and \(\eta_j=\min\{v_j-r_j,\,s_j-v_j\}=\alpha(s_j-r_j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subdivision is a bisection of ratio alpha when it divides a longest side at a point whose smaller distance to the side's endpoints equals alpha times the side length.
assumptions_latex: M=[r,s]\text{ is a rectangle subdivided via }(v,j)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{bisection of ratio }\alpha\iff j\text{ corresponds to a longest side of }M,\ v\text{ lies on that side, and }\min\{v_j-r_j,s_j-v_j\}=\alpha(s_j-r_j)

knowledge_statements.title: Conical Successive Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone-based spatial partitioning for concave minimization over polyhedral regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be a nonempty compact polytope, let \(f:P\to\mathbb{R}\) be finite and concave, and fix \(\varepsilon\geq0\). Represent each live region as \(R=(a+K)\cap P\), where \(a\in P\) and \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a finitely generated convex cone, and associate a valid bound \(L(R)\leq\min_{x\in R}f(x)\) with it. Select a live region and partition its cone into finitely many cones \(K_1,\ldots,K_m\) satisfying \(K=\bigcup_{i=1}^mK_i\). Create the children \(R_i=(a+K_i)\cap P\), evaluate prescribed feasible candidates, update the incumbent value \(U\), and fathom every child satisfying \(L(R_i)\geq U-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition a polyhedral feasible region through finitely generated cones, bound each child, and discard cones that cannot improve the incumbent by more than the tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Every conical split covers its parent, and every node bound is valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The splitting and fathoming operations remove no point \(x\in P\) satisfying \(f(x)<U-\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: polyhedral region induced by the cone

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exhaustive Localization of Conical Refinements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refinement condition required in addition to finite child coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conical partition tree on compact \(P\) is exhaustively localizing if every infinite branch of nonempty compact regions \(R_0\supseteq R_1\supseteq\cdots\), where \(R_k=(a_k+K_k)\cap P\), satisfies \(\operatorname{diam}(R_k)\to0\). For nested nonempty compact regions this is equivalent to the branch intersection being a singleton. Finite child coverage alone does not imply localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every infinite conical branch must shrink to one point; covering every parent is not enough.
assumptions_latex: Branch regions are nonempty, compact, and nested.
Every parent is covered by finitely many child regions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall(R_k)_{k\ge0}\text{ infinite branch},\quad \operatorname{diam}(R_k)\to0.

notation.meaning: Region at depth k on an infinite conical branch.

knowledge_statements.title: Exhaustive Localization of Conical Refinements

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Covering Conical Splits Need Not Localize
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary separating exact child coverage from genuine refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=[0,1]\), \(a=0\), \(K=\mathbb R_+\), and \(R=(a+K)\cap P=P\). At every iteration retain as a child the same conical region \(R\). The child family covers its parent, but the infinite branch has \(R_k=P\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(R_k)=1\). For \(f(x)=x\), the valid bound \(L(R_k)=-1\) and repeated feasible evaluation only at \(x=1\) give \(U_k=1\), so the certified gap remains \(2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A covering conical refinement can retain an unchanged branch and a permanently loose valid bound.
assumptions_latex: Every refinement retains the unchanged region \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{diam}(R_k)=1\quad\text{and}\quad U_k-L(R_k)=2\text{ for every }k.
knowledge_statements.title: Covering Conical Splits Need Not Localize

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence of Fair Localizing Conical Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global convergence under exhaustive localization and consistent regional information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Apply the accepted conical partitioning scheme to a compact polytope \(P\) and continuous concave \(f\). Assume every split covers its parent; every live region whose bound can remain globally minimal is selected fairly; every infinite selected branch is exhaustively localizing; and for a branch \(R_k\downarrow\{x\}\), its valid bounds satisfy \(L(R_k)\to f(x)\) while feasible evaluations on that branch have values approaching \(f(x)\). Then, with \(\underline L_k=\min_{R\in\mathcal L_k}L(R)\), the incumbent satisfies \(U_k-\underline L_k\to0\). Consequently every positive-tolerance gap test eventually succeeds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fair selection, shrinking conical branches, and locally exact bounds and evaluations make the certified gap vanish.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty compact polytope and \(f\) is continuous and concave.
Every conical split covers its parent.
Potentially best live regions are selected fairly.
Bounds and feasible evaluations are consistent under localization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_k-\underline L_k\to0.

notation.meaning: Live conical regions after iteration k.
Minimum valid bound over live regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Convergence of Fair Localizing Conical Partitioning

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exhaustive and Nondegenerate Cone Subdivision Process
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the two defining requirements of an END cone subdivision process.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cone subdivision process is END if the following hold for every infinite nested sequence of generated cones \(\{M_k\}\): (i) \(\{M_k\}\) converges to a ray; and (ii) after translating and rescaling each simplicial polyhedral cone so that its vertex is \(0\), its \(n\) generators are nonnegative and satisfy \(\langle e,\bar z\rangle=1\), let \(B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times\binom n2}\) have as columns the unit directions of the edges of the generator simplex. Then \(\operatorname{rank}B_k=n-1\), and every convergent subsequence \(B_{k_\ell}\to B\) has \(\operatorname{rank}B=n-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An END cone subdivision process is exhaustive, meaning every infinite nested cone sequence converges to a ray, and nondegenerate, meaning no convergent subsequence of the normalized generator-simplex edge-direction matrices loses rank in the limit.
assumptions_latex: \{M_k\}\text{ is any infinite nested sequence of cones generated by the process}
B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times\binom n2}\text{ consists of unit edge directions of the normalized generator simplex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_k\to\text{ a ray},\qquad B_{k_\ell}\to B\Longrightarrow\operatorname{rank}B=n-1

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conical Radial Subdivision Induced by a Simplex Subdivision
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines radial subdivision of a simplicial polyhedral cone through radial subdivision of its generator simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a polyhedral cone with vertex \(x^\circ\) and linearly independent generators \(z^i-x^\circ\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\). Let \(S=\operatorname{conv}\{z^1,\ldots,z^n\}\). A set \(\mathcal{K}_P\) of \(q\leq n\) cones is a conical radial subdivision of \(K\) if there are \(u\in S\) and a simplicial radial subdivision of \(S\) such that, for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(S_j=\operatorname{conv}(\{z^i:i\neq j\}\cup\{u\})\) belongs to that simplex subdivision if and only if the cone \(K_j\), with vertex \(x^\circ\) and generators \(\{z^i-x^\circ:i\neq j\}\cup\{u-x^\circ\}\), belongs to \(\mathcal{K}_P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conical radial subdivision is obtained by radially subdividing the simplex formed by the cone's generator points and replacing each resulting simplex with the cone having the original vertex and corresponding generator directions.
assumptions_latex: K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is a polyhedral cone with vertex }x^\circ
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_j\text{ occurs in the simplicial radial subdivision of }S\iff K_j\in\mathcal{K}_P\quad(\forall j=1,\ldots,n)
