children.title: Degeneracy-Induced Search Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Search inefficiency and stalled refinement attributable to persistent degeneracy.

assumptions_latex: A deterministic decomposition run produces nondecreasing lower bounds \(B_t\), nonincreasing incumbent bounds \(U_t\), and retained cut spaces \(\mathcal C_t\).
Tolerances \(\varepsilon_B,\varepsilon_U\ge0\) and a window length \(q\ge1\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The run is degeneracy-stagnant over \([t,t+q]\) when all subproblems are coupled-degenerate and neither bound nor the cut span changes beyond the stated tolerances.

notation.meaning: Relaxed-dual lower bound and incumbent upper bound.
Linear span of retained cut coefficient vectors.
Number of consecutive iterations in the stagnation window.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational failure boundary; it does not assert that every degenerate run must stagnate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(q\ge1\) and tolerances \(\varepsilon_B,\varepsilon_U\ge0\). A run is degeneracy-stagnant on iterations \([t,t+q]\) if every generating subproblem in that window is coupled-degenerate and \[B_{t+q}-B_t\le\varepsilon_B,\qquad U_t-U_{t+q}\le\varepsilon_U,\qquad \mathcal C_{t+q}=\mathcal C_t.\] Here \(\mathcal C_s\) is the span of retained cut normals after iteration \(s\). The condition records failure to improve either bound or add an independent cut; degeneracy alone, without these consequences, is not stagnation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search is degeneracy-stagnant when consecutive coupled-degenerate subproblems yield no material bound improvement and no enlargement of the cut-normal span.
knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Induced Search Stagnation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed stagnation window, tolerances, and cut-span equality form a bespoke operational failure boundary. No evidence supports this particular definition or its attribution to degeneracy.

children.title: Problem Scaling Imbalance
children.top_down_role: Disparities in variable, constraint, objective, or coefficient magnitudes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Balanced Row Magnitudes Do Not Guarantee Good Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates row-magnitude balance from numerical sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A_\varepsilon=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\1&\varepsilon\end{bmatrix}\), where \(0<\varepsilon<1\), the Euclidean row-norm ratio tends to \(1\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), whereas \(\kappa_2(A_\varepsilon)\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nearly equal row magnitudes can coexist with arbitrarily poor conditioning when the rows are nearly dependent.
assumptions_latex: Row magnitudes and conditioning are measured in the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{\max_i\|a_i\|_2}{\min_i\|a_i\|_2}\to1\quad\text{while}\quad\kappa_2(A_\varepsilon)\to\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Balanced Row Magnitudes Do Not Guarantee Good Conditioning

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint-Row Scaling Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A representation-dependent diagnostic for nonzero constraint rows in a fixed norm; it covers row scaling but not all variable, objective, or nonlinear-function scales named by the leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonzero represented rows \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\), define \(s_i:=\|(a_i,b_i)\|\) in a fixed norm and \[R_{\mathrm{row}}:=\frac{\max_i s_i}{\min_i s_i}.\] Then \(R_{\mathrm{row}}\ge1\), with equality exactly when all represented row magnitudes agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-row imbalance is the largest-to-smallest nonzero augmented-row magnitude ratio in a fixed representation and norm.
assumptions_latex: Every included augmented row \((a_i,b_i)\) is nonzero.
One norm and one formulation representation are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_{\mathrm{row}}:=\frac{\max_i\|(a_i,b_i)\|}{\min_i\|(a_i,b_i)\|}\ge1.

notation.meaning: Magnitude of represented constraint row i.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Row Scaling Imbalance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Row-Imbalance Diagnostics Depend on Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes the represented row-scale diagnostic from an invariant property of the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\) by \(\alpha_i a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le\alpha_i b_i\), where \(\alpha_i>0\), preserves the feasible half-space but changes its augmented-row magnitude from \(s_i\) to \(\alpha_i s_i\). Consequently, \(R_{\mathrm{row}}\) can be changed arbitrarily by equivalent positive row scalings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive row rescaling preserves the mathematical constraints but can arbitrarily change the row-imbalance diagnostic.
assumptions_latex: The row norm is absolutely homogeneous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\}=\{x:\alpha_i a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le\alpha_i b_i\},\qquad s_i'=\alpha_i s_i.

notation.meaning: Positive scaling applied to constraint row i.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Imbalance Diagnostics Depend on Representation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Variable-Domain Scale Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-dependent disparity among positive bounded-coordinate widths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite bounds \ell_j\le x_j\le u_j with w_j=u_j-\ell_j>0, define R_{\mathrm{var}}=\max_j w_j/\min_j w_j. The substitution z_j=(x_j-\ell_j)/w_j maps the represented intervals to [0,1] and makes this width ratio one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-domain imbalance compares the largest and smallest positive coordinate widths; unit-box scaling removes this particular disparity.
assumptions_latex: Every included coordinate has finite bounds and positive width.
The represented coordinate system is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_{\mathrm{var}}:=\frac{\max_j(u_j-\ell_j)}{\min_j(u_j-\ell_j)}\ge1.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Domain Scale Imbalance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normalized Coefficient-Column Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column-magnitude diagnostic after a declared row normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After fixing a row normalization, let c_j=\|A_{:j}\| for every nonzero coefficient column and define R_{\mathrm{col}}=\max_j c_j/\min_j c_j. Under x=Dz, column j is scaled by D_{jj}; hence the ratio depends on variable units and the row-normalization rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column imbalance compares nonzero column magnitudes after row normalization and changes under variable rescaling.
assumptions_latex: A coefficient or linearized-coefficient array A is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_{\mathrm{col}}:=\frac{\max_j\|A_{:j}\|}{\min_j\|A_{:j}\|}\ge1.
knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Coefficient-Column Imbalance

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Declared Objective and Constraint-Function Scale Profile
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensionless profile of represented function variation over a declared reference region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D be a fixed reference region and F_0=f,F_1,\ldots,F_m the represented objective and nonlinear constraint functions. For each included nonconstant F_i with finite positive oscillation a_i=\sup_DF_i-\inf_DF_i, choose a dimensionally compatible reference scale \tau_i>0 and set r_i=a_i/\tau_i. The profile (r_i) and ratio R_{\mathrm{fun}}=\max_i r_i/\min_i r_i are meaningful only together with D and the declared scales; there is no canonical cross-unit ratio without those choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective and nonlinear-constraint magnitudes can be compared using declared dimensionless scales, but the comparison is normalization-dependent.
assumptions_latex: Each included function has finite positive oscillation on D.
Every \tau_i is positive and dimensionally compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_{\mathrm{fun}}:=\frac{\max_i(a_i/\tau_i)}{\min_i(a_i/\tau_i)}\ge1.

notation.meaning: Oscillation of function i on D.
Declared reference scale for function i.

knowledge_statements.title: Declared Objective and Constraint-Function Scale Profile

assumptions_latex: The formulation has nonzero coefficient rows \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\), indexed by \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
Row magnitude is measured in a fixed norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The row-scaling imbalance is \(R:=\max_i s_i/\min_i s_i\ge1\), where \(s_i:=\|(a_i,b_i)\|\).

notation.meaning: Magnitude of the coefficient and right-hand-side row.
Coefficient vector and right-hand side of row i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: coefficient-scale ratios are a standard operational measure of formulation imbalance
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measures row-scale disparity in a fixed representation and norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonzero formulation row \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\), define its magnitude by \(s_i:=\|(a_i,b_i)\|\) in a fixed norm. The row-scaling imbalance is \[R:=\frac{\max_{1\le i\le m}s_i}{\min_{1\le i\le m}s_i}.\] Then \(R\ge1\), with \(R=1\) exactly when all row magnitudes agree. Because multiplying one constraint by a positive scalar changes \(R\) without changing its feasible half-space, \(R\) diagnoses the numerical representation rather than an invariant property of the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Problem scaling imbalance is the ratio of the largest to smallest nonzero constraint-row magnitude in a fixed norm and representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Problem Scaling Imbalance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ratio is a coherent representation-dependent diagnostic, but no source supports choosing augmented row norms or calling this specific ratio problem scaling imbalance.

children.title: Numerical Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity and reliability issues associated with ill-conditioned optimization subproblems.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Matrix Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise sensitivity of a nonsingular local linearized or KKT system, not a global condition number for the nonlinear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular local system \(Kz=r\), its matrix 2-norm condition number is \[\kappa_2(K):=\|K\|_2\|K^{-1}\|_2.\] It measures worst-case normwise amplification associated with solving the represented linear system. Singular matrices are assigned \(\kappa_2(K)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local numerical conditioning measures worst-case normwise sensitivity of a represented linearized or KKT solve.
assumptions_latex: Conditioning is measured in the matrix 2-norm.
\(K\) is the represented local linearized or KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_2(K)=\|K\|_2\|K^{-1}\|_2\quad\text{for nonsingular }K;\qquad \kappa_2(K)=+\infty\quad\text{for singular }K.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Matrix Conditioning

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank-Deficient Active Jacobian Makes the KKT Matrix Singular
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conditioning failure for the standard equality-constrained saddle-point form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix},\] failure of full row rank of \(A\) implies that \(K\) is singular, so \(\sigma_{\min}(K)=0\) and \(\kappa_2(K)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A standard KKT saddle-point matrix is singular when its active constraint Jacobian has dependent rows.
assumptions_latex: The KKT matrix has the displayed saddle-point form.
The active Jacobian \(A\) lacks full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}(A)<\operatorname{rows}(A)\implies \sigma_{\min}(K)=0\quad\text{and}\quad\kappa_2(K)=+\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Active Jacobian Makes the KKT Matrix Singular

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singular-Value Characterization of Matrix Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent 2-norm representations for a nonsingular local linearized or KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonsingular \(K\), \[\kappa_2(K)=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(K)}{\sigma_{\min}(K)}.\] Its 2-norm distance to the set of singular matrices is \(\sigma_{\min}(K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The 2-norm condition number is the largest-to-smallest singular-value ratio, and the smallest singular value is the distance to singularity.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a nonsingular real or complex matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_2(K)=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(K)}{\sigma_{\min}(K)},\qquad \min_{K+E\,\mathrm{singular}}\|E\|_2=\sigma_{\min}(K).

notation.meaning: Largest and smallest singular values of K.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Value Characterization of Matrix Conditioning

assumptions_latex: A local linearized or KKT system is \(Kz=r\) with nonsingular \(K\).
Conditioning is measured using the matrix \(2\)-norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local normwise condition number is \(\kappa_2(K):=\|K\|_2\|K^{-1}\|_2\), and it bounds first-order relative sensitivity to perturbations.

notation.meaning: Nonsingular local linearized or KKT matrix.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normwise matrix conditioning is standard numerical linear algebra
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses local matrix sensitivity, not a global condition number for the nonlinear problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular local system \(Kz=r\), define its normwise numerical condition by \[\kappa_2(K):=\|K\|_2\|K^{-1}\|_2.\] If the matrix is perturbed to \(K+\Delta K\) and \(\|K^{-1}\Delta K\|_2<1\), then sensitivity is controlled by the product of \(\kappa_2(K)\) and the relative perturbation size. A large \(\kappa_2(K)\) therefore means that small coefficient perturbations may produce large relative changes in the computed local solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical conditioning measures how strongly a local linearized or KKT solution can react to small coefficient perturbations.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Conditioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The matrix 2-norm condition number is standard, but the record has no inspectable source for its perturbation interpretation or its use for local KKT systems.

children.title: Scaling-Induced Conditioning Failures
children.top_down_role: Conditioning failures attributable to poorly balanced model scales.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arbitrarily Harmful Diagonal Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact diagonal rescaling can arbitrarily worsen normwise conditioning even when the original matrix is perfectly conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(M>1\), take \(K=I_2\), \(D_r=\operatorname{diag}(M,1)\), and \(D_c=I_2\). Then \(K_s=\operatorname{diag}(M,1)\), \(\kappa_2(K)=1\), and \(\kappa_2(K_s)=M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal scaling can turn the identity matrix into a matrix with an arbitrarily large condition number.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(D_rKD_c)/\kappa_2(K)=M\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: Scaling disparity and resulting condition number.

knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrarily Harmful Diagonal Scaling

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Condition Deterioration Versus Computational Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaling-specific condition deterioration, without asserting a universal finite-precision failure threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be nonsingular and \(K_s=D_rKD_c\) for nonsingular diagonal scalings. Define \(\rho=\kappa_2(K_s)/\kappa_2(K)\). The scaling deteriorates this normwise condition measure exactly when \(\rho>1\). Neither \(\rho>1\) nor a condition-number estimate alone proves failure of a particular numerical algorithm; such a conclusion also depends on the algorithm, perturbations, data, arithmetic, and requested accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling worsens 2-norm conditioning when it increases the condition number, but no condition-number threshold alone proves that a computation fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho>1\iff\kappa_2(K_s)>\kappa_2(K)\), with no universal algorithm-independent failure threshold.

notation.meaning: Ratio of scaled to unscaled 2-norm condition numbers.

knowledge_statements.title: Condition Deterioration Versus Computational Failure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Scaling Preserves the Condition Number
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating harmless scalar multiplication from nonuniform scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(K\) is nonsingular, \(D_r=\alpha I\), and \(D_c=\beta I\) with \(\alpha,\beta>0\), then \(D_rKD_c=\alpha\beta K\) and \(\kappa_2(D_rKD_c)=\kappa_2(K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly multiplying all rows and columns leaves the 2-norm condition number unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(\alpha\beta K)=\kappa_2(K)\).

notation.meaning: Uniform positive row and column scaling factors.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Scaling Preserves the Condition Number

assumptions_latex: The original local system matrix \(K\) is nonsingular.
Positive diagonal row and column scalings \(D_r,D_c\) produce \(K_s:=D_rKD_c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaling-induced conditioning failure occurs when \(\rho:=\kappa_2(K_s)/\kappa_2(K)>1\) and \(u\kappa_2(K_s)\ge1\).

notation.meaning: Condition-number deterioration factor caused by scaling.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the product of condition number and unit roundoff is a standard reliability indicator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient diagnostic boundary, not a claim that every nonuniform scaling worsens conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_s:=D_rKD_c\), where \(D_r\) and \(D_c\) are positive diagonal scaling matrices, and define \[\rho:=\frac{\kappa_2(K_s)}{\kappa_2(K)}.\] The scaling is condition-deteriorating when \(\rho>1\). It enters the stated finite-precision failure regime when, additionally, \[u\kappa_2(K_s)\ge1.\] In this regime the usual small-perturbation condition-number estimate cannot ensure even one reliable relative digit. Values \(\rho<1\) instead indicate that the chosen scaling improves this particular normwise condition measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling causes a conditioning failure when it worsens the local condition number enough that its product with unit roundoff reaches one.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Induced Conditioning Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source justifies defining failure at unit-roundoff times condition number equal to one. That threshold makes a standard estimate noninformative but does not itself prove computational failure, while the plain statement is more categorical than the qualified LaTeX statement.

children.title: Finite-Precision Reliability Limits
children.top_down_role: Limits on numerical discrimination, feasibility assessment, and bound reliability under finite precision.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-Based Forward-Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori reliability certificate for a nonsingular local linearized or KKT solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Kz=r\) with nonsingular \(K\), let \(\widehat z\) be an approximate solution and \(\rho=r-K\widehat z\). Then \[\|z-\widehat z\|_2\le\|K^{-1}\|_2\|\rho\|_2.\] If \(r\ne0\), then \[\frac{\|z-\widehat z\|_2}{\|z\|_2}\le\kappa_2(K)\frac{\|\rho\|_2}{\|r\|_2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual certifies forward accuracy only after accounting for inverse-norm or condition-number amplification.
assumptions_latex: Residuals and norm bounds are evaluated with validated error control.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|z-\widehat z\|_2\le\|K^{-1}\|_2\|r-K\widehat z\|_2.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Based Forward-Error Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Small Residual Can Coexist with Large Forward Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that residual magnitude alone is not a reliability certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon)\), \(r=0\), and \(\widehat z=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}\), where \(0<\varepsilon<1\). The exact solution is \(z=0\), while \(\|r-K\widehat z\|_2=\varepsilon\) and \(\|\widehat z-z\|_2=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ill-conditioned system can have an arbitrarily small residual at a point with order-one solution error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|r-K\widehat z\|_2=\varepsilon\to0\quad\text{while}\quad\|\widehat z-z\|_2=1.

notation.meaning: Small positive singular value and residual scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Small Residual Can Coexist with Large Forward Error

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Backward-to-Forward Error Reliability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise matrix-only backward perturbation bound for a nonsingular local linearized or KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Kz=r\) and \((K+\Delta K)\widehat z=r\), where \(K\) is nonsingular and \(\|\Delta K\|_2/\|K\|_2\le\delta\). If \(\kappa_2(K)\delta<1\), then \[\frac{\|\widehat z-z\|_2}{\|z\|_2}\le\frac{\kappa_2(K)\delta}{1-\kappa_2(K)\delta}.\] When \(\kappa_2(K)\delta\ge1\), this perturbation bound supplies no finite forward-error guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For matrix-only backward error, a finite normwise forward-error bound requires the condition number times the relative perturbation to be below one.
assumptions_latex: The computed solution exactly solves the matrix-perturbed system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_2(K)\delta<1\implies\frac{\|\widehat z-z\|_2}{\|z\|_2}\le\frac{\kappa_2(K)\delta}{1-\kappa_2(K)\delta}.
knowledge_statements.title: Backward-to-Forward Error Reliability Boundary

assumptions_latex: The exact system is \(Kz=r\) with nonsingular \(K\).
The computed solution satisfies \((K+\Delta K)\widehat z=r\) with \(\|\Delta K\|_2/\|K\|_2\le\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\kappa_2(K)\delta<1\), then \(\|\widehat z-z\|_2/\|z\|_2\le\kappa_2(K)\delta/(1-\kappa_2(K)\delta)\); no such bound follows when the product reaches one.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: backward-to-forward error conversion is standard perturbation theory
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise backward-error boundary for a nonsingular local linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Kz=r\) and the computed vector \(\widehat z\) exactly solves \((K+\Delta K)\widehat z=r\), where \(\|\Delta K\|_2/\|K\|_2\le\delta\). If \(\kappa_2(K)\delta<1\), then \[\frac{\|\widehat z-z\|_2}{\|z\|_2}\le\frac{\kappa_2(K)\delta}{1-\kappa_2(K)\delta}.\] When \(\kappa_2(K)\delta\ge1\), this perturbation argument provides no finite forward-error guarantee. Thus finite precision cannot certify solution reliability from backward stability alone beyond that boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A backward-stable solve has a finite forward-error guarantee only while the condition number times the relative backward error remains below one.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Reliability Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated matrix-perturbation bound is standard but uncited. The plain statement overgeneralizes it to all backward-stable solves, whereas the LaTeX assumptions fix the right-hand side and perturb only the matrix.

assumptions_latex: There are \(W\) workers and a coordinating master in \(d\) variables.
Workers generate \(K\) previously unknown dense cuts \(a_k^{\mathsf T}z\le b_k\).
Communication transmits explicit scalar coordinates without shared generative compression.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact reconstruction of all generated cuts at the coordinator requires transmitting \(K(d+1)\) scalar coordinates, hence \(\Theta(Kd)\) scalar communication.

notation.meaning: Number of newly generated dense cuts.
Dimension of the coordinating master vector.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-transmission bound for centralized collection of explicit dense cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(W\) workers generate a total of \(K\) previously unknown dense affine cuts \(a_k^{\mathsf T}z\le b_k\) for a coordinating master with \(z\in\mathbb R^d\). Under explicit scalar-coordinate transmission, reconstructing every cut at the coordinator requires communicating its \(d\) coefficients and one right-hand side. The total payload is therefore \[K(d+1)=\Theta(Kd)\] scalar values, in addition to synchronization metadata. This bound does not apply when cuts have a shared sparse, parametric, or otherwise compressible representation already known to the coordinator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Central collection of K previously unknown dense cuts in d variables requires transmitting K(d+1) scalar coordinates under an explicit-coordinate communication model.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Coordination Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordinate count follows from the stipulated dense explicit-transmission model, but no source supports presenting it as a distributed coordination limit. The complexity-bound kind otherwise fits the quantitative statement.

children.title: Distributed Communication Limits
children.top_down_role: Restrictions imposed by latency, bandwidth, message volume, or unreliable information exchange.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Communication Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A transcript-counting lower bound for deterministic distributed GOP coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a deterministic distributed implementation whose coordinator must distinguish among \(M\ge 2\) pairwise distinguishable global states. If the complete worker-to-coordinator transcript contains at most \(B\) bits, correctness on every state requires \[B\ge \lceil\log_2 M\rceil.\] More generally, if coordination must distinguish all \(2^k\) combinations of \(k\) independent binary branching decisions, then at least \(k\) communicated bits are necessary in the worst case, irrespective of the number of workers or their local computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinguishing M possible global states requires at least ceiling(log2 M) communicated bits; parallel local computation cannot remove this information requirement.
assumptions_latex: The distributed protocol is deterministic and must be correct for every admissible global state.
The \(M\) states require pairwise distinct coordinator decisions or certificates.
Communication cost counts all bits received by the coordinator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\ge \lceil\log_2 M\rceil\).

notation.meaning: number of pairwise distinguishable global states
worst-case communicated transcript length in bits

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. The GOP Approach: Distributed Implementation p. 243

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. The GOP Approach: Distributed Implementation p. 243

The transcript model must also specify fixed-length, prefix-free, or padded transcripts for the stated counting argument. A source directly supporting the communication model and bound is required.

children.title: Communication-Constrained Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination regimes whose effectiveness is restricted by the available communication environment.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Constrained Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-robust termination condition for distributed lower-bound coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(t\) be the communicated transcript, let \(\Omega(t)\) be the set of problem executions compatible with \(t\), and let \(U(t)\) be the value of a communicated feasible incumbent. For each active region \(r\in\mathcal R\), let \(\ell_r(\omega)\) be a valid lower bound in execution \(\omega\). The transcript permits certified \(\varepsilon\)-global termination exactly when \[U(t)-\inf_{\omega\in\Omega(t)}\min_{r\in\mathcal R}\ell_r(\omega)\le \varepsilon.\] Thus an uncommunicated region prevents termination whenever some compatible execution assigns it a lower bound below \(U(t)-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Limited communication permits termination only when every execution consistent with received messages has a global lower bound within epsilon of the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The active region set \(\mathcal R\) is finite and common to all compatible executions.
Each \(\ell_r(\omega)\) is a valid lower bound on region \(r\).
The incumbent underlying \(U(t)\) is feasible and \(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U(t)-\inf_{\omega\in\Omega(t)}\min_{r\in\mathcal R}\ell_r(\omega)\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for active region r

children.title: Distributed Scalability Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Loss of distributed performance as coordination overhead or communication burden dominates useful computation.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Scalability Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential branching defeats distributed scaling when no leaf can be pruned.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(K\) independent binary branching decisions producing leaves \(s\in\{0,1\}^K\). A known feasible incumbent has value \(1\); each leaf oracle reports either that the leaf is empty or that it contains a feasible point of value \(0\), with at most one such leaf. For any \(0\le\varepsilon<1\), a deterministic method requires \(2^K\) oracle resolutions in the worst case to certify \(\varepsilon\)-global optimality. With \(p\) workers resolving at most one leaf per round, at least \(\lceil2^K/p\rceil\) rounds and \(2^K\) aggregate leaf reports are required in the no-improving-leaf instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without pruning, K binary decisions create 2^K leaves; parallelism reduces rounds by at most p but leaves aggregate work and reports exponential.
assumptions_latex: The \(2^K\) leaves cannot be eliminated by dominance, relaxation bounds, or symmetry.
An unresolved leaf remains compatible with containing the unique value-zero feasible point.
Each worker resolves at most one leaf per coordination round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{\mathrm{leaf}}\ge 2^K\), \(R_p\ge\lceil2^K/p\rceil\), and \(C_{\mathrm{reports}}\ge2^K\).

notation.meaning: number of independent binary branching decisions
